clean_body: LA Times: California election experts sound alarm as rate of rejected ballots quadruples| | | Stats like this from California are the canary in the coal mine, Team. Kern County went from 332 uncounted, late ballots in 2024 to 3,303 in 2025. In Riverside County it was almost 6,000 uncounted, late ballots, more than double 2024's total.Remember: These are from eligible voters, postmarked on time, sent ahead of or on Election Day. They should have counted -- except Trump's changes to the USPS made them arrive too late. = | | | | = Here's the deal, Team: Due to USPS changes, a huge number of mail-in ballots arrived too late to be counted in last year's special election in California. A review by the Los Angeles Times showed that "ballots came in late at an average rate four times higher than that of the 2024 election." By California law, vote-by-mail ballots are considered late if they do not arrive within seven days of election day, even if they are postmarked on or ahead of election day. What does this mean? There is now concrete proof that Trump's changes to the U.S. Postal Service are aiding his attacks on mail-in voting. California voters did their job and mailed their ballot in accordance with their laws. Trump's attacks on the Postal Service aren't letting them deliver those ballots on time. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | | = | | = | | | = | | = | | = | | | Election officials warned before that 2025 special election that the Postal Service changes could delay the postmarking of ballots and lead to votes not being counted. Trump's USPS leadership shrugged after reducing the number of post office pickups in a quest for "efficiency". “ Something changed ,” said Melvin E. Levey, who heads the Merced County Registrar of Voters. “ We don’t like seeing late ballots and if someone has made the effort to vote, we want to count it.” Semi-rural Merced County saw almost a sevenfold increase in late-arriving mail ballots in the November election compared with the year before. We have to make sure every voter understands this change and how it can impact them \-- from vote-by-mail, to bills, taxes, legal replies to companies, so much more. name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Trump is refusing to sign our housing bill that passed. I’m fighting back.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
Congress actually passed something good.

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2940%2E4032634%2EPOQFwB)
---
I don’t say this often these days, but Congress actually passed something good. We just overwhelmingly passed the most substantial housing bill in more than 30 years. My 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act would lower housing costs, build more homes, help working families afford rent and homeownership, and prevent private equity firms from scooping up homes that families could own. Republicans were even boasting about it this morning — saying what a great bill it was. It was ready to become law this morning. And then, suddenly, Donald Trump threw a tantrum and refused to sign it. Why? Because he's demanding Congress pass the SAVE Act first — the restrictive voter ID law that would make it harder for millions of citizens to vote. Or as Donald Trump said, "guarantee the midterms" for the Republicans. | [](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3683?t=8&akid=2940%2E4032634%2EPOQFwB)
---
[**Trump is blocking relief for millions of families struggling to afford rent and buy a first home because he wants leverage to force through his extremist voter suppression bill. But make no mistake: I will not stop fighting to get this signed. Will you chip in $28 right now to fuel our fight?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3683?amount=28&t=9&akid=2940%2E4032634%2EPOQFwB)

I need to make this abundantly clear: We are in a housing emergency. People across this country are saying that housing is at the top of their list of costs that they are struggling with. Passing this bipartisan bill showed that even when Democrats are in the minority, we can get stuff done and deliver lower costs for American families. We got everyone on board to bring down costs, crack down on corporate landlords and private equity firms buying up neighborhoods, and put homeownership back within reach for working families. Even Donald Trump said himself that he supported this housing bill. The White House even called it "one of the most significant pieces of housing affordability legislation in American history." Then the President just turned around and acted like a petulant child the minute it’s time to sign the bill. We can laugh and joke about his dramatics, but this is serious. This is really serious for the young family that can't buy a home. This is really serious for the renter who sees his rent going up again and just doesn't know how he's going to cover both health insurance and rent. This was a serious effort to lower costs, and Donald Trump won’t sign it for political games. [**No games. No theater. No tantrums. I’m calling on Trump to sign this bill immediately — and I won’t let up in this fight. If you're able, will you pitch in $28 or any amount to power our campaign?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3683?amount=28&t=15&akid=2940%2E4032634%2EPOQFwB) Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth

July 21 starts the clock on the most important governor's race in the country. |
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133957146/629639358/-1397648958?refcode=AU_AZD_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260624_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS8xMDU1MTYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZjc3NGZjMzQtMmE3MC1mMTExLWFjOWMtMDAwZDNhNTRiZWQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=56482wQM2ZQBe-1IJzfl1cZgu8mUVZLRjuoTTO9MfyE=)

Team, Our end of quarter deadline is right around the corner. Here’s what we’re working towards:
* **Protect our Democratic trifecta** — defending our Governor, Secretary of State, and Attorney General.
* **Expand our state legislative map** to ensure fair representation in every corner of the state.

Friend, Deb Haaland here. We are living through a defining moment. This November, across the country — right here in New Mexico and our neighboring state Texas — elections will determine whether we fight for our values or allow extremism and chaos to take hold.
**We are facing real issues that demand real leadership, and that's why I'm reaching out today._[Will you split a contribution of $5 between Gina Hinojosa's campaign for Governor of Texas and my campaign for Governor of New Mexico?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5897?refcode=jtk950-bu-nd&amount=5&t=2&akid=10542%2E400544%2E6PD7NH)_**
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Gina Hinojosa and Deb Haaland will go through immediately:_ | | | [Donate $10 >>](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/8813?refcode=jtk950-bu-nd&t=3&akid=10542%2E400544%2E6PD7NH)

Across the country, Democratic governors are leading the fight to lower costs, expand opportunity, protect healthcare, strengthen public schools, and stand up for working families. Together, we have the opportunity to elect two more Democratic governors who are ready to deliver this November.

I'm running for Governor because New Mexico deserves leadership that will tackle the challenges families face every day and build a future where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.
And in neighboring Texas, my friend Gina Hinojosa is running to fight for strong public schools, affordable healthcare, lower costs, and a state government that works for working people.

Sound familiar?
Friend, the truth is that what happens in Texas affects New Mexico, and vice versa. Our states share a border, but we also share families, workers, businesses, and communities. The decisions made by Texas leaders can have consequences that ripple across our entire region.
For years, Texans have lived under Republican leadership that has put politics ahead of solving problems. Texans deserve better. And New Mexicans deserve a partner next door who is focused on expanding opportunity, protecting freedoms, and delivering real results.
Gina and I believe in the same future for our states: One where working families can get ahead, where every child has access to a great education, where healthcare is within reach, and where the government works for people. **_I know Gina and I will be strong partners in that work._**
**But this partnership won’t be possible without you, friend.[If you're ready to help elect governors who will fight for working families across the Southwest, please split a contribution of $5 — or whatever makes sense for you — between our campaigns today. Every donation helps us reach more voters, build stronger campaigns, and compete against well-funded Republican opponents.](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5897?refcode=jtk950-bu-nd&t=7&akid=10542%2E400544%2E6PD7NH)**

---
Thank you.

Be Fierce,
Deb

| | Today marks 4 years since the Supreme Court overturned _Roe v. Wade_. Four years since reproductive health care and bodily autonomy were ripped away from millions of Americans. This was the biggest strike in a generation against the constitutional right to privacy in our country. And the Trump administration has been eager to build on this crusade against reproductive freedom wherever possible. Trump has rescinded guidance that protects emergency reproductive care in hospitals. He pardoned anti-choice protestors who'd been found guilty of harassment and violence outside of health clinics. He revoked Defense Department funding for service members who need to travel to receive reproductive health care. Meanwhile, his enablers in Congress continue to legislatively chip away at reproductive rights. **Republicans' "One Big Beautiful Bill" included – among its many horrible features – a complete defunding of Planned Parenthood for the year. Since then, clinics have shut down, and women have been left without the health care they need.** But there's one fundamental truth that anti-choice Republicans forget:**the American people don't sit quietly when their rights are taken away.** Time and time again over the last four years, we've seen record turnout in down-ballot races against anti-choice extremists. Voters in "red" states such as Montana, Ohio, Kentucky, and Kansas have defeated abortion bans or passed abortion protections. Last year in Wisconsin, with abortion rights potentially on the line, the GOP's effort to retake the State Supreme Court failed spectacularly (with their candidate losing by _ten points_). There is a path to restoring reproductive freedom _everywhere_ in America – and it starts with flipping the Senate in November. If we do that, we can stop any piece of anti-choice legislation in its tracks and block Trump from appointing more anti-choice judges. **And when a Democratic administration (hopefully) takes office in 2029, our congressional majorities will be ready to immediately codify the rights that**** _Roe_****granted.** Our fight ahead won't be easy, but it can be won. Freedom is a powerful thing – and voters in red, blue, and purple states alike want it. So let's get to work. [**Will you join me? **Peter, Donald Trump is leaving people behind.**
The President is _refusing_ to sign landmark affordable housing legislation with wide bipartisan support unless he gets his extreme voter suppression bill.
[](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260624-2.CVeDXA&refcode=em-20260624-2&t=2&akid=1541%2E1086043%2EjCdkxU)

We need to know one thing...
Peter,November is closer than you think, and 2026 is shaping up to be the most important election of our lifetime.Here's the deal: **House Republicans have been getting it DONE.** We **codified** President Trump's Executive Orders into law. They want to undo every single win we've fought for -- your tax cuts, your border security, your energy independence._**If we lose this majority, it all gets erased. We have to keep building on this momentum, every single day, all the way to November.[**Click HERE to take our Official 2026 Turnout Tracker and tell us what's got you fired up this election season.**](https://timmoore.cmail20.com/t/y-l-foohl-hkhielhuy-i/) [CHIME IN HERE](https://timmoore.cmail20.com/t/y-l-foohl-hkhielhuy-d/) We will win -- because we MUST win -- to save America.Thank you, Congressman Tim Moore

| Dear Friends,

Every year families work harder, yet take home less.
Every year government grows larger and more expensive.
And every year the same politicians promise solutions while the problems only get worse.

**Enough is enough.**
In the video above, Jerrod Sessler delivers a direct message: Washington, D.C. created this mess, and it's time for real leadership that will cut the waste, stop the reckless spending, and put America first again.

That's exactly why Jerrod is running for Congress.

He's bringing the **[Rescue Washington](https://sendmanage.jerrodforcongress.com/send1/l/cRwY2WMZosKKG664LUBf1w/JyEIyHxr4WsVEdTiOGwF2w/nv1d3cD9t4hxoO3vSvHMJA)** plan to the table -- a practical strategy focused on protecting working families, restoring fiscal sanity, and delivering the common-sense representation our district deserves.

With ballots arriving in **just three weeks** , we're entering the most critical phase of this campaign. The final push to reach voters and secure victory in the August primary will take every resource we can muster right now.

We have an opportunity to change that.
This race is one of the most competitive congressional races in the country, and national Democrats will spend millions trying to keep this seat. If we're going to win, we need conservatives across Northwest Ohio to step up and help us build the resources necessary to communicate our message and turn out voters.

# Thursday, June 25, 2026
---|---
**Good Morning!** On this day in 1876, Native American forces led by Crazy Horse and Sitting Bull defeated the U.S. Army troops commanded by Lt. Col. George Armstrong Custer in [the Battle of the Little Bighorn](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOozAQhJ8GOiN7wcAVLq6hy7VXosVeh42MHdlOEG9_SnRv8HcjfdLM6Pt7W2_IgeP9Dx5kqk9rpLMEqpXyGl82EGaO5Um2cooFD8pscQUJo5CjAL065HCtQ-uMJwLqWzJqmqGfQSnd7sZ7qUerZ2X9pAacQeIvpSYcJ9t71_ctm0-bHEErKeded94N47Z50hI9zvPUDJIc15S7R-JYd_LhSm_KnU1HG8xe67M0_e8GlgaW8zy7nUtN-frwBpa6cxEOL8FR_CcNLI9XJAG6gWXDWgOJ5EXgb9r4vqcc22zc8-QQuIyfD_cDOXw3649EvQ38CwAA__9CiX41), located near the Little Bighorn River in southern Montana. Yale just tracked over 11,000 seniors for more than a decade, and what they found breaks every rule you've been told about getting older. Nearly half of them didn't decline. They got BETTER. | | | Last week was Juneteenth. It's always a highlight of the summer. For me, Juneteenth is a joyful celebration of family, resilience, perseverance, and strength. This year, I saw families holding reunions centered on their hometown Juneteenth celebrations. We visited five celebrations, two in Opelika and one each in Auburn, Lanett, and Lafayette. We came home tired every night, but it was worth it. We met hundreds of people at those events, and in every instance, people were warm and receptive, and I think, just a little surprised to see a congressional candidate at a small-town celebration. We had the chance to show people we care about all of these communities by showing up and listening to them. Some seemed skeptical when we said we would be back, but we will be, because that's what this campaign is all about.

---
While the economy has boomed, workers have been left behind. The Economic Policy Institute has shown that since the 1970s, the economy has expanded and American workers' productivity has increased significantly, while workers' compensation has lagged behind for 40 years.
I started thinking about this a few weeks ago, when employees at an Alabama Starbucks voted to unionize. What caught my attention was how many people on social media were furious that Starbucks employees would have the nerve to expect better wages and working conditions from a company that turned a $1.8 billion profit last year... and yes, I said $1.8 BILLION IN PROFITS. There seemed to be a general consensus that any increase in workers' compensation would trigger an economic cataclysm.
We should talk a bit about the minimum wage, what it was supposed to be, what impact raising it will have on employment, and what effects it will have on small businesses...

📰 [Summer Heat Drives Energy Use Higher for Alabama Households; New Tools Available to Help](https://swo5c8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001x2x2E38gO6upRI1Rd9wYreTM1UuKtl7axOuIQAbvLgVayDfICNlprzBiM1E8Wq3rKt6j6gO5N8-sTYDhmIqAe0d2j7B_t5vfpXwaBrHdqo1mTVIcE-yJuVgDzGacqChFxNrGNIvaczkjI740G9c98Zv7rofQYgbdhxb8PF6fIzrubdSfRKtZIk7Ve1qUmbize6y7NDSyDHdqOAPzi-GAxcMk6gCyQo090unEBZEs1F44TaTCYZDVBB93mukn7vk8BDdqTYFsPZPCzMkRm2S1DQ==&c=toIL2SglXcRRfYPnFyMu5N25PXuAlPrBmlsC_26iQTDvFusQOoR0ew==&ch=kOgOdGLrAym_AU-kU4Jom3zba2f4gYNqA8vQ0jrpAq7bXx0A6o5ONg==)
As summer temperatures rise across Alabama, households may see higher electric bills primarily because increased air conditioning use drives up energy consumption, not because of higher utility rates. Alabama Power says heating and cooling account for up to half of a home's electricity use and has introduced a new online tool, TempCheck, to help customers understand how extreme temperatures affect energy demand. The company also recommends energy-saving practices and offers resources to help residents manage seasonal utility costs.

Project Red Clay, a proposed $1.5 billion artificial intelligence data center in Lowndes County, would span 800 acres near Hayneville and could bring thousands of construction jobs and up to 200 permanent positions to the area. The project reflects Alabama's growing role in the rapidly expanding data center industry, but it has also sparked local opposition, with residents raising concerns about energy use, water consumption, community input, and the long-term impact on the rural county. Developers say the facility will be fully responsible for infrastructure costs and have pledged $10 million in community investments if the project moves forward.

📰 [Only 1 in 10 Alabama voters showed up for the primary runoff as years‐long decline continues](https://swo5c8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001x2x2E38gO6upRI1Rd9wYreTM1UuKtl7axOuIQAbvLgVayDfICNlprzBiM1E8Wq3r09qdFKyThsgO8nAecvkKDonGBgK_v4L7mVvFcGvJXvYB_dLvkRSi1edn5E8HrsRFvgHYx8BDlnoqoWvS-4IyAoDnIRSFnCXejHJySiPgHLbvuJr4AifHKUyjrMeF4d-pqKgARY27HXDIAhaN-hl7BXbxZF6eySaVYB5n829VShmt3qWs0LqVg4sBP3vwPY4yMmXkGn9-uFZAmCWy8t1n948RdCZK6xQ9Toj2g9DY1EH4w4RjP9Fa7Q==&c=toIL2SglXcRRfYPnFyMu5N25PXuAlPrBmlsC_26iQTDvFusQOoR0ew==&ch=kOgOdGLrAym_AU-kU4Jom3zba2f4gYNqA8vQ0jrpAq7bXx0A6o5ONg==)
Only 10.7% of Alabama's registered voters participated in the 2026 primary runoff election, continuing a years-long decline in runoff turnout across the state. Fewer than 466,000 of Alabama's 3.6 million registered voters cast ballots, marking a drop from the 12.8% turnout recorded in the 2022 runoff election. The low participation rates highlight ongoing concerns about voter engagement and civic participation, particularly in elections held outside of presidential cycles.

# One Last Thought Until Next Week
---
| | |
---
We're taking some time to finalize our plans for the next phase of the campaign, and we need your help.
There will be many events throughout the district over the summer. We can't know where and when they'll all be, so let us know if your town is hosting a block party, Food Truck Thursday, big farmers' market, 4th of July celebration, Founders Day, or any gathering where we can come say hello. We don't need a table; we'll just come, pass out cards, shake hands, and let people know who we are and what we're running for.
You can email the team event information at [joinus@leemcinnis4alabama.com](mailto:joinus@leemcinnis4alabama.com). We look forward to seeing you in the district this summer.
One campaign staff announcement: As we enter the final months of the campaign, it's clear I need to shift some responsibilities. I have asked Barbara McInnis to serve as the Campaign Chief of Staff. While some of you may think it's because communication is easy since we live together, that's not the main reason. clean_body: You Don't Want to Miss This | | | | | == | | | CAMPAIGN UPDATE | | | | | | == | MAKING HISTORY | | THE WEEK AHEAD | | Cleburne County Democrats Monthly Meeting 🗓️ June 25 🕓 6 P.M. 📍 937 Ross St. Heflin, AL 36264 | | Pell City Town Hall Meeting 🗓️ July 9 🕓 6 P.M. - 8 P.M. 📍 Details Coming Soon | | | THE WEEK BEHIND | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Last week was Juneteenth. It's always a highlight of the summer. For me, Juneteenth is a joyful celebration of family, resilience, perseverance, and strength. This year, I saw families holding reunions centered on their hometown Juneteenth celebrations. We visited five celebrations, two in Opelika and one each in Auburn, Lanett, and Lafayette. We came home tired every night, but it was worth it. We met hundreds of people at those events, and in every instance, people were warm and receptive, and I think, just a little surprised to see a congressional candidate at a small-town celebration. We had the chance to show people we care about all of these communities by showing up and listening to them. Some seemed skeptical when we said we would be back, but we will be, because that's what this campaign is all about. | | | | | | | | | | | | In Case You Missed It | BLOG POSTS | == While the economy has boomed, workers have been left behind. The Economic Policy Institute has shown that since the 1970s, the economy has expanded and American workers' productivity has increased significantly, while workers' compensation has lagged behind for 40 years. I started thinking about this a few weeks ago, when employees at an Alabama Starbucks voted to unionize. What caught my attention was how many people on social media were furious that Starbucks employees would have the nerve to expect better wages and working conditions from a company that turned a $1.8 billion profit last year... and yes, I said $1.8 BILLION IN PROFITS. There seemed to be a general consensus that any increase in workers' compensation would trigger an economic cataclysm. The company also recommends energy-saving practices and offers resources to help residents manage seasonal utility costs. | 📰 == Project Red Clay, a proposed $1.5 billion artificial intelligence data center in Lowndes County, would span 800 acres near Hayneville and could bring thousands of construction jobs and up to 200 permanent positions to the area. | This is a breathtaking level of open corruption and the Supreme Court of the United States made it possible.
The Supreme Court's immunity ruling didn't just protect Trump from prosecution for January 6th. It handed him the legal architecture to run a government that answers to no one, to use the Justice Department as his personal law firm and the United States Treasury as his personal ATM.
The fund is administered by acting Attorney General Todd Blanche, Trump's former personal defense lawyer, who now controls the Justice Department that negotiated the deal. The commission that decides who gets paid was appointed by Blanche. Trump can fire any of them at any time. There is no independent oversight and no congressional approval.
And the federal judges who will hear every legal challenge to this fund? Trump's judicial nominees who refused under oath at their Senate confirmation hearings to say Trump lost the 2020 election.
Let's say that again. The judges ruling on the legitimacy of a fund created to compensate people who tried to overturn that election will not say that Trump lost that election.
Trump is not paying these people because he feels bad about what happened to them. He is paying them because he needs them operational for 2026 and 2028. Lindell built the election denial infrastructure MAGA needs to challenge Democratic votes at scale. Tarrio built the street-level operation for when institutional channels fail. The 1,600 pardoned January 6th defendants are the army Trump needs on standby when he declares the next election rigged.
The immunity ruling made the payment legal and the packed courts will make sure the plan is executed. Unpack Our Courts exists to stop that from happening. We are building the movement to reform and rebalance the Supreme Court -- the court that made this slush fund possible and will rubber-stamp everything that follows. The state court firewall holds the line while we build the political will to fix the court at its source. Upcoming events and recap of the Special Session
| | | | | [](https://a89bm49ab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001KHzJ04CjI-ZuA331XyDZF6BNCJUHa6i6zm4lCcCKnMU7izbiw4qgiZ_qViDLO8bs_f0iewBegrh5g6C8G2vE02seopc_yV3osy_woQoQygRBEdXxt3wkurwh74hdivkammI-k7zuNXl6yRC3gcgvJNN8ipNIFRES&c=0RfRZtENWsMpEfWaqc4z4DacTUC36pwTFjWvVJk1LpPs7DIMxreJFA==&ch=tsR93kwezzAXtzNg1dhUMvjNYxktTicGGRwiSYPKkjU7czWBNx5M4Q==)

| Onto November
Last week marked the end of Georgia's primaries with the runoffs. Georgia voters have now selected the nominees to represent both parties in November. In the Republican primary, we had tough races up and down the ticket with many strong candidates. Like most people, not every candidate I supported won -- but now it's time to unify and come together as a team. I'm supporting our entire Republican ticket, and I hope you will join me. I look forward to welcoming our nominees to the district in the coming weeks and months.
Last Tuesday was also an important night for Athens, as we rejected socialism and ensured Athens will not have a socialist mayor for the next four years. It is hard to believe we have to celebrate something like that, but we do -- especially after seeing what is happening in places like New York.
With all of these races now behind us, it means our campaign can kick into high gear for the general election in November. I ask for your continued support and prayers as we get back on the campaign trail. If you are interested in hosting or attending a meet & greet, roundtable, or fundraiser, please contact Caitlyn Dill at [caitlyn@houstongaines.com](mailto:caitlyn@houstongaines.com).
Read below for a recap from the recent Special Session under the Gold Dome, as well as updates from the campaign.
---
|
---
Special Session Recap
---
| | |
---
The Georgia General Assembly returned to the State Capitol on June 17 for a special legislative session called by Governor Kemp. The session focused on several limited issues included in the Governor's proclamation, including election law, local homestead tax exemptions, and ratification of the temporary suspension of motor fuel taxes. In a special session, the legislature can only take up the items outlined in the Governor's call.

During the special session, the General Assembly passed House Resolution 3EX, which ratified the governor's executive order temporarily suspending Georgia's motor fuel and diesel fuel taxes. While the Governor can suspend the gas tax by executive order, the legislature must approve this action the next time it is in session.

The legislature also passed Senate Bill 3EX, which makes updates to Georgia's election law and voting system requirements. While this legislation didn't have everything we wanted, it addressed a looming July 1 deadline by extending the timeline for implementing certain ballot tabulation changes that the Secretary of State failed to do. Had this not passed, the courts would've stepped in, leaving our election law in limbo and in the hands of federal judges. Importantly, the bill also creates a committee to develop recommendations for a new uniform election equipment system ahead of the 2028 election cycle.

Two issues that were part of the Governor's proclamation but that didn't receive final passage were local property tax relief legislation and redistricting. Democrats in the State House and Senate were able to block property tax legislation as these changes require a super majority to pass. While the U.S. Supreme Court made it clear Georgia must redistrict to ensure our maps are in line with court orders, this will be done at a later date since it did not pass during the special session.

The special session concluded on Tuesday after five legislative days.
| |
---
| Events In The District
Even with the primary behind us, we haven't slowed down over the last month. We've been making campaign stops throughout the district and state including the Oconee County GOP Stumping Ground, the retirement ceremony for Colonel Mike England (35 years with the Dept. of Natural Resources) and Major Doyte Chaffin (31 years with Dept. of Natural Resources), the Georgia GOP Rodeo, and many more. See below for a few photos from recent events.
If you have events you'd like us to attend or groups you would like us to speak to this fall, please let us know!

## Camp Mystic Files for Bankruptcy
Camp Mystic filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on Wednesday, nearly a year after the Guadalupe River flood that killed 27 campers and counselors at the all-girls Christian camp. In paperwork filed in [Houston federal court](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFypTAMBuDTQCfG6GHgFS62ocu2WzICy8ETgRnbCeH2O35b7AHSSqNf-vTnbX4jL_54_007m_ztwnzwlYRz5jivtJ_7nbJfFzo-4ueZ13v3VmhGhT2oHlDPlrzcc1dbsyj7bGs27TDiY9SPAevNLE_Cbhk1Wuf6EcmR6jSOrdaL6ml0tTclTPWo21ahbptxtYqHrhu6p20VDlWn2PocYpM3zvxNyckdvjg2a9hrMVvOZ6oevyqcKpyu62rWJRVF6Vc4vUYqnEqpwqmg4J8KnBdO4EKE_0A4mKLcQHAzRSCXOYJlsnLDKwqchGAT5I0yfHgRtlBCOSZYw-eRWEIsm-po7Hl5EZ_6onjfycvr6PyzV38Z_BsAAP__xvCXfw), the century-old camp listed more than $10 million in debt and assets of no more than $500,000. Camp director Dick Eastland also died in the flood. The filing follows months of hearings in which lawmakers and victims' families faulted the camp's flood planning and its decision to keep girls in cabins as the river rose. Camp Mystic [withdrew its 2026 license application](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFywyAMBuCnwRs-LINxBoYubOna0YeNSLhg4wMax2_fIx36AF206CT9n76u09X44Lfbp1lRlZeL04ZHDlgKpmkx676eufhlNtsjfe9lOVdvg5mAwUDZQEFM1vhwTryxamb20jWoOjlCP4peQnNXYoQRBRdLL3rHpB1HaS4Lnwc7OzbLvvGqLmMDiK5jILp2XCxDybnkF9sxkIQztL7E1JY7FnyZ7MIZn5jaJa5NUPdS9kz6DwKagD6Oo31kU2qTgK4aAvo9RkDXUwQ0qwU4AV2J9NdInQ-YqYuJ_nGpCWvMhcYN6YkmUeMKJmrR2HBSF2K0BHSTlN0PH4LPQ817W40P73jlf099KvgJAAD__4a-i5o) in April after the first public hearing. Nine families have sued state health regulators, who licensed the camp two days before the flood [despite the absence](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkTuu2zAQRVcjdTSo0c8uWKRR99KmFEbkyB6EIhVyZD3vPqC9hNfd-eAAB_fP1_yF7Dncf-NGRr7XOAc6sycRSrPFbd9eWdguGP6mYxf72th5nEHDoPSgoJ8dsn_NXe3Mot2tqck04xXaa9-OUD_MqFuA221YhrYfwNmGcB2v_dIsOCzOtTWbAtMD9E2joW8uV-s0jV03djfXaBirTpNjiekiDxL6xrz6V3xSuti41d48RPZctb8qmCqYzvO8HLlIlHMFU4kVTAtlUVlQqExvTAUTJmHr36uPEihoK5iKufqoqx0TBckqH_QBKLT2yBzu6o1RcV3ZMvqSVIiiKKwx2fJAT7QHCsegdo9BJfp3cKKNgtTJuP1k7zkPxfG-Ifu3kvysiKeB_wEAAP__kFOg7w) of a required evacuation plan.
## Texas Water Plan Hits $174 Billion
Texas water officials told lawmakers Tuesday that the state's water plan includes approximately $174 billion in proposed projects, but funding sources for many of those projects have not yet been identified. Customers are likely to face higher bills before new funding arrives. SWIFT, the state's main water-infrastructure fund, [couldn't meet demand](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2ypDAMhE8DmaaM-A8INiF7m25IeWwxoxpjU5beY7j9FpPsATaVurv66z9fy5flwPHx22406XtNS6RDAqlSXpzd9u0UZXe38ZW_d3Xnxj7YBQ12YDrAdvGWw7k0pZ_uxo9VSVPVD1gPbd1j-ZzGe11Xten82g9jQ22Lg62bbmwq17ajwZKnK8x02FaVwba6Dc4b6pumb0ZfGeyLxpBnTfmmT1J6W1nDmX4o31zayjA9VXcp6l8FzgXOx3HcXm8br2eB80VT4PyxwZ4CK7t_h8MqZUjryo5tEBCiF2wpE6zf0XN8gBVwmYUFjpSFooBLogKSbAZ9sgALxKTwSJdcE4imvcC5zJPfDw6BpbsQHpvl8Gms_7fzz4R_AwAA__-aNpUb) for the first time in 13 years, covering less than half the cost of approved projects. Voters approved $1 billion a year for water projects last year, but that money [won't be available until 2028](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLvS2yAQRp8GdWhgdS8o0qhz2pSaFaxkHBAawJb19hnZeYO_3NuZs9-f23RD6-y2_kZPKr-XMG10JEc5U5w0-t2fKVs94_Y3PvesT2-NwwkEtFy0HJrJoHXnVBdGzcIMsiAlux6qvqk6KO6qqxZoSSAt2C1UyUGi1PNVQ9v2ZiisumCihUZKAY0se20EdXXd1YORAjpWCzI2h1jmO2V6Y1rcGV4USx184dQ95z2x6heDkcF4HEe5zdosxzVmMF7_MBhd0OgYjB8A_988MFPks3UucY8nt5uOhIk4Jv5dTDk-19VR4jnw5bkZ7vERIv9e7jE8SOcLVYv6smcwFlGZ_bDO2dRe8qtH6z6u-WcJvxT8CwAA__8GwJI_), so utilities are expected to pass along rising costs to ratepayers in the meantime. Officials pointed to data centers as a major new driver, with the number of surveyed data centers [jumping from 22 to 341](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OpDAQhJ8Gsh4Z82MICC4h20svRB67gdb6B7l7Z5a3P7GvsHGVPlV9_z7WD0uB0v7XRpzle8trwjcHFMGyOhvPeLGQe9r0Wb5OcVckH-yqlR5ADaD71VsK19rVfn4qPzU1zo0ZdTv2rdH1MVuln2rYnujQbcMw9r0f3YTjZHpjusbVNN8wNei-aZTum8fovELTdaabfKO0qTqFniSXhxwo-G15C1d-YXm4HOswHyInV-2fSi-VXuTAg0K4s0ovZw7krkovmLDsF2B6UckpYpJKL_3UmrZr4AcKbytYIG8bObKBgRE_IeaCsH0lT2kHy-AKMTG8c2FMDC6zMHC2BeQgBmJIWWDPd10ysOSz0ktdZn--KQTi4f6zR0s_E2v5nfTXrP8HAAD__1rrmjw) in two years. Some lawmakers urged caution on the price. Rep. Trent Ashby, R-Lufkin, said the state may need to recapitalize SWIFT but wanted clarity on how much to commit.
## Most Texans Oppose Local Data Centers
A new [University of Texas poll](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OnEAQhJ8GskbD8HsBgZPNzqlD1PQ0u-2bHzTT7N2-vbW8gsMqlT5V1Z_P9RPFS7z_xsCL_uxpjfxdPKtyXgnDEV5FhTaMX_k8lF5BnMfVGjuCGcEOq0Pxr7Wv3bIZ99HWvLTTbLt56CZbP5Z52jo70kQjotsNdW7fZ2OJaLKI21DL8oaZ0Q5ta-zQNjM5w1PfT_2Ha42dqt6wE0250Qcr_2DZ_Ss9OTeUQu2Xh-pRqu5XZW-VvV2BI3lRodKcl2zYnZW9bT7dK3v7e0aGI3kPu0RXAIFSOFhF5clwQoHCEZUhIzFIhIsBGMQBpagST4l3YEoxBaG3R5xjAYeKQByVM2xIXx7Lo86LO77Feynje8k9oPiruP7f3c_F_gsAAP__sN6aag) found that 56% of Texans oppose building a data center in their own community, against 29% who support it. Opposition runs highest in rural Texas, where 62% are against a local data center. Those are the same counties where [most projects are planned](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uwzAMhJ_G3hTI9G8GDV28pWtHg5boWCgtCRabxG9fuAX6At0I8HD33X3cpht69uH-jhsZeS1xCvTMTCK0Txa3tB1ZvJ0xfO5fSeyxecc4gYZO6U5BOzn0fExN6cys3bUqyVT9APXQ1j2Uq6EaYNHXFuxARJWdF-toxmEYuh5nrUtvTjPdQVtVGtrqMlinqW-avrm6SkNfNJqcl7hfZCWhF-aFj_ig_WLjVrJZRVIu6rcCxgLGjAHDnTiyf9CpKGA8KxUwpshevD3PP_7m961SZFZ5jc-stphFnTkhq5hSzKQcCipLQWjP5W5cenpmn7uT7b6h5x8U-d-ADwPfAQAA__-vCoaU), thanks to lower land costs and lighter local oversight. The split crosses party lines: [71% of Democrats](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL0SnCAURp9GOxy4omhBkcZu06Z0EK67JPw4cHdd3z5jXiH9mTPn-3491ofxwafnTxNR03fPa8KzBiTCsloTj3hV8nYz6U95H2Sv6F0wK3AYGR8ZDKszPlyrbJ3euJtFi1qoCfpp6BW0Lz3P2EvcDRqQVu1869U0bLArMYLshWq9vmV8hEEIDoPoJus4KimVnJ3goBrJ0XnKpaMXEn5N3cOVP1g6m2Mb9IvoqE3_o4GlgeU8z27PX2XelXy6kQaWe1MDSzS_c_F0sduSKsvHkSsyZ8gwi4mwVGZzjO90Q8baXJxPT5bwZEcOoS3aHacPwdfxznpG48O_Cvq_7z4a_gYAAP__oJGGkw) and 62% of independents opposed a nearby center, while Republicans were divided at 44% opposed and 42% in favor. Texas is set to be the nation's top data-center market, a build-out backers tout as a job and tax-revenue generator. Gov. Greg Abbott has [urged limits](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL8GMpDdGAyBg0vI5tILUWP3DNbZGNm9w_D3K_YXNi7Vq9L791ge6IPfX38xkuHPMy07nSUQM-XFYjziVdjbFff_-etge0XvAi4gYGjE0EC_OPThWlTtzCrcJGsyUo_QjX2nod4MjJLQ4tStINRq9UqdI-loWnspwKnamxsmBuilFNDLdrROkFZKq8lJAbpSgpznlFveiOmD5Rmu9Kbc2hTrYDbmo1TdnwrmCubzPFtM4c4qmDGzt4FKBXNMhZu7vpcmHUcq1DhkbCztTLk0crwXez20G8dQZ-OO04fgy3A_eEX0P9Caf6fpbeA7AAD__26EfPk) on the centers' water and power use and an end to their sales-tax break. James Henson, who directs the poll, said the Legislature is likely to act in January.

The SAVE Act on the other hand, is the most sweeping voter suppression law in American history. It would disenfranchise millions of voters, disproportionately Black and minority voters. Dan Cox for Governor, Thank you for your support and vote. We won! Watch our event last night [here](https://us.list-manage.com/NnMX5mHdS7w?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b).

body:
Join Dr. Nila Devanath for an evening of community, conversation, and support in Virginia Beach.
| |

PEOPLE-FIRST LEADERSHIP FOR VIRGINIA'S 2ND
Dear Friend, You are invited to join us for a **Desi Community Fundraiser** in support of **Dr. Sudipta “Nila” Devanath, M.D., J.D.,** Democratic candidate for Congress in Virginia’s 2nd District. This will be an evening of community, conversation, and support as we come together to meet Dr. Nila, hear why she is running, and help build the people-powered campaign needed to carry this message forward. _**Event Details**_**Dr. Nila Devanath for Congress Desi Community Fundraiser****Date:** Friday, June 26 **Time:** 6:00 PM – 9:00 PM **Location:** 1314 Kempsville Rd **CLICK BELOW TO RSVP:****
****_[RSVP HERE](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1XXqxUazRWwn-6wLTo9PZPlW-BP9l7WaSCSpi9-rTsJs/viewform?edit_requested=true)_****
****Dr. Nila** is a physician, attorney, mother, and community advocate who is running because families in Hampton Roads and across Virginia’s 2nd District deserve leadership rooted in service, compassion, and real-life experience.Campaigns are expensive, and every contribution helps us reach more voters, organize more volunteers, share Dr. Nila’s message, and keep this campaign moving strong through the final stretch. **
****Donate to Dr. Nila for Congress**[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/nilaforcongress](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/nilaforcongress?refcode=email)
You can also learn more about Dr. Nila and the campaign here: [https://niladevanath.com ](https://niladevanath.com)
We hope you will RSVP, attend, bring a friend, and help show strong community support for Dr. Nila. With gratitude, **Dr. Nila For Congress**
* * *
* * *
Will you chip in today to help us win this race? Every dollar helps us reach more voters. | | [CHIP IN $50 NOW](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/nilaforcongress?refcode=email&amount=50)

I have dedicated my life to sharing America’s greatest stories through films. They examine crucial moments in our nation’s history and the threats to our democracy. These stories are not easy.
Today, our country is facing its own reckoning, and the stakes have never been higher.
That is why I am reaching out. Alex Vindman—who I first met in 1983 while filming my documentary, _The Statue of Liberty_ , when he was seven—is running for the United States Senate. Alex is an amazing American and a true fighter for what is right. He’s a man of character.

name: DNC Headquarters
subject: You deserve to know…
body:
We might have to make some tough decisions.
---
Derek, You deserve an explanation. You’re going to be seeing us in your inbox a bit more often over the next few days, and we wanted to let you know why. We know your time is valuable, and we wouldn’t email you if it wasn’t important. Our end-of-quarter fundraising goal is coming up, and we set an ambitious goal here at the DNC: **_We need to raise $750,000 by Tuesday night.**_ That may seem like a lot, but $750,000 isn’t an arbitrary number for us. Our team set that goal intentionally to ensure that we have the resources to power Democrats to victory this November, so we cannot afford to miss it. **If we come up short, we’ll have to make some tough decisions** , like hiring fewer organizers to register new Democrats to vote or sending less money to state parties. **We’re not going to let that happen, but we need your help to make this work. Right now, we’re falling short. So, we’re reaching out to our top supporters and asking: [**If winning this November is important to you, please chip in $7 to the DNC today. We’ll put your donation to work immediately to elect Democrats up and down the ballot, all across the country.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-eom-june-2026?refcode=em_20260625_7721_fr&amount=7&refcode2=7721_22930333_YUknUX&akid=7721%2E22930333%2EYUknUX)** _If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly._ | | | **[Donate $7](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-eom-june-2026?express_lane=true&amount=7&refcode=em_20260625_7721_fr&refcode2=7721_22930333_YUknUX&akid=7721%2E22930333%2EYUknUX)**

name: Sen. Jacky Rosen
subject: I'm leading the charge in the Senate to combat antisemitism
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Rosen for Nevada
body:
We must stop the epidemic of antisemitic violence and harassment.
| | |
---
Friend,
I am the third Jewish woman and the first former synagogue president ever elected to the United States Senate. Think about that: In our nation’s 250-year history, there were only TWO Jewish women elected to the Senate before I joined.
Like any believer, my faith is deeply tied to who I am, what I fight for, and my role as a lawmaker. It’s part of why I care about the issues that I do, and it means that I bring with me the same struggles that all Jews face. Most prominently, the threat and impact of antisemitism.
**That's why I'm leading the charge in the Senate to combat the increasing levels of violence and harassment Jewish Americans are facing right now.**
[**_Will you please make a gift of $5 or more to support my work in Washington to fight the epidemic of antisemitism across our country?_**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133961971/629688242/910177728?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=jtk5812-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiMTQwYWUxOC04ZTcwLWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2E1NGJlZDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=VO91R01J7nijL8qf8zbEOdW3o8Fgzo8I8cNdpD_4sSU=)
| | [Donate $5](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133961972/629688243/1781803786?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=jtk5812-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiMTQwYWUxOC04ZTcwLWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2E1NGJlZDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=VO91R01J7nijL8qf8zbEOdW3o8Fgzo8I8cNdpD_4sSU=)
---
For me, this fight is personal. When I was just a few years old, I was playing in a hotel swimming pool with my mom while on vacation when a lifeguard on duty told her that we were “dirty” because we were Jewish – and that we had to leave the pool immediately because of it. My parents packed up our things and left that hotel. We never returned. My mom never forgot that interaction, retelling the story for years.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133961973/629688244/1781803786?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&refcode=jtk5812-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiMTQwYWUxOC04ZTcwLWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2E1NGJlZDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=VO91R01J7nijL8qf8zbEOdW3o8Fgzo8I8cNdpD_4sSU=)
Nearly every Jewish American has a moment in their lives when they experience or witness antisemitism like that firsthand, and the problem is especially serious today.
Swastika graffiti. Physical assaults and threats. Firebombings. **Multiple** deadly mass shootings. These attacks on Jews are not isolated incidents. They represent a regression toward one of civilization’s darkest chapters.
All of it is wrong, and addressing this kind of violent antisemitism is an issue I’ve been working on since before I came to Congress and throughout my time in the House and Senate. **That is why:**
* I founded the Senate’s first ever Bipartisan Task Force for Combating Antisemitism, which now includes more than half the Senate as members.

* I just introduced the _Jewish American Security Act –_ sweeping legislation to fight antisemitism on college campuses, at Jewish communal institutions, and online. The bill is supported by the American Jewish Committee, the ADL, and the Jewish Council for Public Affairs.

* I successfully pushed the Biden administration to create the first-ever National Strategy to Counter Antisemitism, which took a whole-of-government approach to tackling rising hate.

* I led the effort in Congress to increase the power of the State Department’s Special Envoy to Monitor and Combat Antisemitism by raising the position to the rank of Ambassador.

* I introduced and successfully helped pass legislation reauthorizing the _Never Again Education Act_ to educate communities about the Holocaust.

* I successfully pressured the Trump administration to avoid weakening Coast Guard standards for hate symbols like swastikas.

When I think about this work, I think about being that little girl with her mom again. Every day, I'm trying to help make our country a place where nobody is targeted because of their faith or who they are – whether it’s at a swimming pool, on a college campus, or in the United States military.
**This work is more urgent than ever now that Americans across the country are being targeted, attacked, and killed simply because they are Jewish. body:
Voter ID Goes to Washington, Again

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/grantdemocracy/grant-report-june-25-2026?e=c16f400a56)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/u29DIbiENmy?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a)
| | **Voter ID Goes to Washington, Again****By Justin Riemer, President, USGI, and Marshal Trigg, Counsel, USGI** The [introduction of the Voter ID Act](https://us.list-manage.com/PGCKnKAqnHY?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) last week marks the latest effort by Congress to set national rules for verifying voter eligibility. Introduced by House Administration Committee Chairman Bryan Steil, the legislation would require voters to provide identification when casting a ballot in federal elections, either in-person or by mail. The bill looks designed to address the most common criticisms of both recent federal legislation such as the SAVE America Act and voter ID requirements more broadly. Opponents argue that ID requirements may burden voters who lack government-issued identification. To assuage these concerns, the legislation would authorize federal grants to support states’ issuance of free ID cards, provides for an affidavit exception for those with a religious exemption, and would permit voters without ID to cast provisional ballots rather than being turned away outright. It also permits mail voters to list the last four digits of their Social Security number on their ballot return materials in lieu of a photocopy of their photo ID so long as they attest to being unable to obtain a copy of one after making reasonable efforts. The Voter ID Act is also more narrowly tailored than other measures now before Congress that include voter ID provisions such as the [SAVE America Act](https://us.list-manage.com/bF3lRsp11P7?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) which would also require documentary proof of citizenship (“DPOC”), and Congressman Steil’s own more comprehensive [MEGA Act](https://us.list-manage.com/fjaK6BEk7XZ?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that encompasses a federal overhaul of mail voting, ranked-choice bans, and voter list maintenance changes. The Voter ID Act touches only on verifying ID. For example, opponents of the SAVE America Act have focused on alleged difficulties associated with married women and young voters securing DPOC and less on its voter ID provisions. Narrowing the focus to voter ID narrows the target and may improve its odds of passage. Although a national standard would at least partly preempt preexisting state ID laws, including in states that already have a strict photo ID requirement like Texas, there are undoubtedly benefits to national uniformity instead of the patchwork of rules in place now. Election officials can coordinate public education efforts on a nationwide basis, as could political parties and nonprofit groups. Interstate movers would also have the benefit of having consistent rules instead of learning the nuances of their new state’s voter ID requirements. Requiring photo ID to vote is [broadly popular](https://us.list-manage.com/_HCsjFG2QwE?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a). Indeed, recent [research](https://us.list-manage.com/1932HrpH8CE?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) supported by the Grant Institute suggests it bolsters confidence in the electoral process and the legitimacy of those elected. Whether it can clear a closely divided Congress is another question. Perhaps at a minimum, it can serve as a starting point for achieving the type of consensus needed to clear the high bar for passing meaningful legislation in the modern Congress.
---
| | | | |
---
| | **Alaska** The Division of Elections made a final ruling of [ineligibility](https://us.list-manage.com/QcIhKwAlVbW?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) for a primary challenger to Senator Dan Sullivan. The challenger, also named Dan Sullivan, was determined to have not filed his candidacy in good faith. The Division of Elections cited that the challenger is registered to vote under the name Daniel J. Sullivan, Jr.; an email requesting ballot access as Dan S. Sullivan, the incumbent senator’s name; and registration as a Republican only just before filing to run. The challenger has [appealed in state court](https://us.list-manage.com/zahxEMT1SX3?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a).**Arizona** The state legislature [passed](https://us.list-manage.com/11NXSjP6Wb_?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) HCR 2001 on June 12 along party lines. The passage places a measure on the state’s general election ballot for approval that would require all voters to provide “valid government issued proof of identity” including for mail-in ballots. If passed by voters, the measure would take effect in 2028.**Arkansas** The State Board of Election Commissioners [voted](https://us.list-manage.com/tD8Y_1i8Lbz?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) to petition the U.S. Supreme Court following a ruling from the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals holding that the state’s “wet-signature” rule was not material to determining voter qualifications. The rule prohibits the use of e-signatures for voter registration and requires a “wet-signature” on a piece of paper. The Eighth Circuit’s ruling creates a circuit split as both the Fifth and Eleventh Circuits have found similar provisions to be material and serving a legitimate state interest. The Board has until August to formally file their appeal.**California** The Los Angeles City Council [approved](https://us.list-manage.com/lK3y_2bhaJt?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a ballot measure that would allow for noncitizen voting in local elections. The proposal would allow for residential-based voting in city and district elections, and will be voted on in the November 3 election. Los Angeles would join cities such as San Francisco and Washington, DC in allowing for noncitizen voting if the measure passes.**Delaware** The legislature [rejected](https://us.list-manage.com/TJCPALyy2tv?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a same-day voter registration bill, which fell short of the required two-thirds majority. Twenty-two states currently allow same-day registration.The state House [passed](https://us.list-manage.com/VzbiqA9HCYp?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) HB 180, a constitutional amendment that would allow for the restoration of voting rights to felons after their sentences have been served. The bill will now go to the Senate for consideration. As the bill is a constitutional amendment, it would require two consecutive legislatures to pass it before coming into effect.**Georgia** The General Assembly [reconvened](https://us.list-manage.com/qJ3eaLrszgW?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) for a special session called by Governor Kemp to address the state voting system ahead of a July 1 deadline barring QR-code ballot tabulation, for which no replacement has been established. The legislature [passed](https://us.list-manage.com/195VTWOdsqG?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) Senate Bill 3EX, which extends that deadline to January 2028, creates a committee to recommend specifications for a new statewide system by January 31, 2027, limits the Secretary of State’s role in selecting it, and expands the contests subject to risk-limiting audits. The bill requires hand recounts in governor or lieutenant governor races decided by [0.5% or less](https://us.list-manage.com/2MsgvNLeyY2?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a). It now goes to Governor Kemp for signature.The General Assembly declined to take up [redistricting](https://us.list-manage.com/pkt1awBJZBS?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) in the special session. Leaders in both chambers expressed that they felt the special session did not give enough time to properly pursue the matter, choosing instead to delay until regular session.**Hawaii** Governor Green [signed](https://us.list-manage.com/MPr5DzYwgqU?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) Senate Bill 2239 into law on June 18. The law will implement automatic voter registration beginning January 1, 2027 tied to applications for or updates to the state driver’s license. The state previously used an opt-in system for voter registration, but under the new law will implement an opt-out system for voter registration.**Maine** State election officials [delayed ranked-choice runoff tabulations](https://us.list-manage.com/yH1f0TNIa0r?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) in the gubernatorial primaries and the 2nd Congressional District Democratic Primary after encountering discrepancies in a small number of ballots. **Maryland** State officials [removed](https://us.list-manage.com/YOPTk2H33OS?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a Guyanese national unlawfully present in the country from its voter rolls. The man had registered to vote in 2011 and re-registered in 2017 following removal for inactivity. The state had initially resisted calls to remove the man from the voter rolls, but did so after he was convicted of gun charges and lying about his citizenship status to obtain a school superintendent position in Iowa.**Michigan** The state Bureau of Elections [removed](https://us.list-manage.com/pOqQXsTeRLP?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) an Antrim County Clerk’s access to voter rolls after allegations she changed or cancelled voter registrations. Maintenance of qualified voter rolls is the responsibility of city and township clerks, and the Bureau alleges that the clerk overstepped her authority and responsibilities by altering or sending notice of cancellation to voters. The clerk has previously cited a “mandate” from voters to clean up the county’s rolls. The clerk is also under [investigation](https://us.list-manage.com/10f7FHTpAsD?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) for an incident involving her husband’s unsupervised access to secure areas of the County Clerk’s office. **Minnesota** A state election judge [pled guilty](https://us.list-manage.com/ym9FpeL_lll?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) to accepting 11 ballots from unregistered voters during the 2024 election. The guilty plea led to a felony conviction with a stayed one-year prison sentence. The judge will serve five years of supervised probation and is barred from serving as an election judge in the future.**Missouri** A county clerk stated that Missouri’s [redrawn](https://us.list-manage.com/e34PLA2qHed?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) congressional districts will be used in the state’s primary election. The clerk had previously resisted switching to the new maps, pending the Secretary of State’s decision on a referendum that would make the districts subject to a statewide vote.**Nevada** Churchill County [misassigned](https://us.list-manage.com/gMkxfLvCEdK?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) 881 Fallon voters to the wrong ward, issuing them ballots that omitted the City Council Ward 1 contest. County officials notified the city, and the city council voted to hold a special election on July 21 to resolve the issue.**North Carolina** A state House committee [approved a sweeping elections bill](https://us.list-manage.com/ADCC0Q10CxE?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a). The latest version would, among other things, bar State Board of Elections and county board members from supporting or opposing candidates or encouraging turnout, require the State Auditor to audit all 100 counties over a six-year period, raise the campaign-finance reporting exemption so fewer contributions and expenditures are disclosed, and remove “never-resident” overseas voters from the definition of eligible voters. The bill would also lengthen the wait before party-switchers can run under a new affiliation.**Ohio** The FBI conducted a [raid](https://us.list-manage.com/7D2tpucjY1S?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) of an Ohio voter registration group as part of an ongoing fraud investigation. In addition, the FBI sent agents to interview employees and staff of the organization at their homes. In 2017, a paid canvasser of the organization pled guilty to a fraudulent voter registration scheme. The organization denies any impropriety in its actions.**Oregon** Governor Kotek’s office [stated](https://us.list-manage.com/CWG61zOhc1q?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that the governor was not considering mid-decade redistricting. Previous redistricting efforts in the state have led to Republican walkouts from the state legislature.**Texas** The state has [assumed](https://us.list-manage.com/721Vrd5uNhF?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) administrative oversight of voter registration in Val Verde County. This comes after county officials repeatedly failed to maintain accurate records according to the state’s mandatory audit. The state did not indicate how long the oversight was expected to last, but mentioned that a full report was expected by July.

The Photo ID Rules (08 NCAC 17 .0101, .0109) align certain deadlines with statutory deadlines and would make a county board’s decision on an in-person or absentee photo-ID exception affidavit a majority-vote matter rather than a unanimous one. The Absentee Voting Rules (08 NCAC 18 .0201–.0505) set procedures for county staff reviewing returned absentee ballots, distinguishing curable deficiencies, non-curable deficiencies that require cancellation and reissuance, and irregularities that do or do not require contacting the voter. The Recount Rules (08 NCAC 09 .0110) change the deadline for when a county board must begin a hand-to-eye recount. The Voting Site Rules (08 NCAC 10C .0101–.0104) address buffer zones, electioneering areas, and conduct, including noise, at voting sites.

clean_body: Voter ID Goes to Washington, Again | | | | | | | | | Voter ID Goes to Washington, AgainBy Justin Riemer, President, USGI, and Marshal Trigg, Counsel, USGI The last week marks the latest effort by Congress to set national rules for verifying voter eligibility. Introduced by House Administration Committee Chairman Bryan Steil, the legislation would require voters to provide identification when casting a ballot in federal elections, either in-person or by mail. The bill looks designed to address the most common criticisms of both recent federal legislation such as the SAVE America Act and voter ID requirements more broadly. Opponents argue that ID requirements may burden voters who lack government-issued identification. To assuage these concerns, the legislation would authorize federal grants to support states’ issuance of free ID cards, provides for an affidavit exception for those with a religious exemption, and would permit voters without ID to cast provisional ballots rather than being turned away outright. It also permits mail voters to list the last four digits of their Social Security number on their ballot return materials in lieu of a photocopy of their photo ID so long as they attest to being unable to obtain a copy of one after making reasonable efforts. The Voter ID Act is also more narrowly tailored than other measures now before Congress that include voter ID provisions such as the which would also require documentary proof of citizenship (“DPOC”), and Congressman Steil’s own more comprehensive that encompasses a federal overhaul of mail voting, ranked-choice bans, and voter list maintenance changes. The Voter ID Act touches only on verifying ID. For example, opponents of the SAVE America Act have focused on alleged difficulties associated with married women and young voters securing DPOC and less on its voter ID provisions. Narrowing the focus to voter ID narrows the target and may improve its odds of passage. Although a national standard would at least partly preempt preexisting state ID laws, including in states that already have a strict photo ID requirement like Texas, there are undoubtedly benefits to national uniformity instead of the patchwork of rules in place now. Election officials can coordinate public education efforts on a nationwide basis, as could political parties and nonprofit groups. Interstate movers would also have the benefit of having consistent rules instead of learning the nuances of their new state’s voter ID requirements. Requiring photo ID to vote is . Indeed, recent supported by the Grant Institute suggests it bolsters confidence in the electoral process and the legitimacy of those elected. Whether it can clear a closely divided Congress is another question. The Recount Rules (08 NCAC 09 .0110) change the deadline for when a county board must begin a hand-to-eye recount. The Voting Site Rules (08 NCAC 10C .0101–.0104) address buffer zones, electioneering areas, and conduct, including noise, at voting sites. | | | Alaska Sullivan v. State of Alaska, Division of Elections, No. 3AN-26-07485 (Alaska Super. Ct.) On June 22, Daniel J. Sullivan, Jr., suit against the State Division of Elections over primary ballot access. The Division of Elections ruled him ineligible for ballot access in a primary race against incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan, stating that the filing was not in good faith.Arizona Heap v. Galvin, No. 1 CA-CV 26-0446 (Arizona Court of Appeals Division One) On June 18, the Arizona Court of Appeals a lower court ruling dividing election administrative duties in Maricopa County prior to the July 21 primary. The court cited the Purcell principle commonly used in federal courts to prevent significant electoral changes prior to elections. The Maricopa County Recorder stated that he would appeal the decision to the state Supreme Court.Arkansas Arkansas United v. Thurston, No. 5:20-cv-05193 (W.D. Ark.) On June 22, the U.S. Supreme Court to plaintiffs, leaving an Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals ruling in place which held that no private right of action is contained in Section 208 of the Voting Rights Act.California State of California v. Shasta County, No. C106517 (Cal. Ct. Appeal, Third Appellate District) On June 12, state Attorney General Shasta County over the passage of a ballot measure the state contends violates state election laws. Shasta County voters passed Measure B, a ballot measure that would require voter ID, hand counting, and restrict mail-in voting. The Attorney General states that the county does not have the authority to make these types of changes, and they would come into conflict with state laws, while the county contests the measure could be altered to come into compliance with existing law. The Shasta County Board of Supervisors voted unanimously to Measure B in the lawsuit.District of Columbia League of Women Voters v. U.S. Department of Homeland Security, No. 25-3501 (D.D.C.) On June 22, a federal court changes made by the federal government to the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) system. The changes were made pursuant to an executive order directing DHS and SSA to create a database that would allow states to quickly verify citizenship of individuals registering to vote. The court ruled that the changes implemented failed to meet congressionally mandated privacy protections and infringed on individuals’ voting and privacy rights.Georgia In re Georgia Senate Bill 202, No. 1:21-mi-55555 (N.D. Ga) On June 12, a federal court to temporarily block parts of Georgia Code § 21-2-414 restricting gifts, including food and water, from being given within 150 feet of a polling location. Plaintiffs sought a preliminary injunction to prevent the relevant sections from being enforced during the primary election runoffs on June 16.Dolezal v. Raffensperger, No. 26CV007174 (Fulton Cnty. Super. Ct.) On June 12, a state court granted a to dismiss an emergency petition seeking to compel the Secretary of State to grant access to the state voting operations center to political candidates during election counting. The court noted that all counting is done at the county level and the state operations center serves only as the official publisher of vote tabulations.Republican National Committee v. Hancock, No. 26-A-05660-7 (Gwinnett Cnty. Super. Ct.);Republican National Committee v. Allen, No. 26CV008750 (Fulton Cnty. Super. Ct.) On June 18, the Republican National Committee Fulton County and Gwinnett County alleging both counties created additional ballot drop-off locations in violation of state law. Additionally, the suits allege the counties created an additional means of ballot return by allowing absentee ballots to be delivered to poll workers in addition to the allowed drop-boxes or designated officials.Maryland United States v. DeMarinis, No. 1:25-cv-03934 (D. Md.) On June 22, a federal court granted a to dismiss with prejudice the federal government’s lawsuit seeking to obtain the state’s unredacted voter file. Massachusetts California v. Trump, No. 1:26-cv-10810 (D. Mass.) On June 24, a federal court the federal government from implementing President Trump’s executive order that would require proof of citizenship when registering to vote. The decision converts an earlier preliminary injunction into a permanent injunction.California v. Trump, No. 1:26-cv-11581 (D. Mass.) On June 18, a federal court that states had standing to sue the federal government over President Trump’s Executive Order 14399 impacting mail-in voting. The states are seeking to enjoin the order prior to the 2026 election, and the court ruled that the case was ripe for review. Michigan Republican National Committee v. Benson, No. __ (Mich. Ct. Cl.) On June 23, the Republican National Committee the Michigan Secretary of State over recently promulgated election rules. The suit alleges the rules violate state law by allowing the number of election challengers in polling places to be lowered below the statutory threshold, denying common conveniences to challengers, and restricting the ability to observe certain processes.United States v. Benson, No. 1:25-cv-1148 (W.D. Mich.) On June 24, the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals that the Department of Justice cannot compel the state of Michigan to turn over its unredacted voter list under the Civil Rights Act of 1960.Minnesota Minnesota Voters Alliance v. City of Minneapolis, No. (Minn. Sup. Ct.) On June 11, the Minnesota Voters Alliance the City of Minneapolis alleging that the city does not intend to appoint party-balance election judges for early voting in 2026. State law requires election judges to be appointed for early voting and that the judges be party-balanced. The city also failed to appoint election judges during the 2024 election.Nebraska Republican National Committee v. Evnen, No. CI 26- (Dist. Ct., Lancaster Cnty.) On June 22, the Republican National Committee against the state regarding a law that allows for U.S. citizens who have never resided in Nebraska or the United States to vote in Nebraska elections provided one parent is registered to vote in the state. The lawsuit argues this violates the state constitution’s provision that voters must have resided in the state and county in which they register to vote.Oklahoma Public Interest Legal Foundation v. Ziriax, No. 5:26-cv-01440-HE (W.D. Okla.) On June 16, the Public Interest Legal Foundation (PILF) filed a against the State of Oklahoma seeking to compel disclosure of the state’s voter roll. Oklahoma state law prohibits the disclosure of the voter roll to non-residents, which PILF contends violates the public disclosure requirements of the National Voter Registration Act.Virginia King v. O’Bannon, No. 3:23-cv-408 (E.D. Va.) On June 18, plaintiffs a motion to enforce a prior judgment, asking a federal court to order expedited compliance with its earlier ruling that Virginia may disenfranchise only for the common-law felonies recognized in 1870 under the Readmission Acts. The state has 14 days from the filing to respond.Wisconsin Bothfeld v. Wisconsin Elections Commission, No. 2026AP001168 (Wis. Supreme Ct.) On June 11, the Wisconsin Supreme Court agreed to hear a second to the state’s current congressional maps, which argues that the current maps are drawn illegally for partisan advantage. A three-judge circuit court panel had dismissed it in March as too similar to previous failed challenges before the high court took it on appeal. | | | | President Trump a scheduled signing of the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, stating he would not sign it until Congress passes the SAVE America Act, which would require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections. The housing bill had cleared both chambers. The SAVE America Act has not advanced through the Senate.On June 18, House Administration Committee Chairman Bryan Steil , which would require photo identification to vote in federal elections, with driver’s licenses, passports, and military IDs among the accepted forms. Mail and absentee voters could attach a copy of their ID, voters who forget theirs on Election Day could cast a provisional ballot, and a new Election Assistance Commission grant program would reimburse state and tribal governments that provide free IDs to voters who cannot afford one.The Department of Homeland Security of state homeland-security grant funding on the adoption of specified election changes, including moving toward hand-marked paper ballots and running voter rolls through the SAVE citizenship database. People often ask me what was going through my head when the President of the United States called for the death of me and five colleagues for making a video he didn't like.
Well, I wish I could say I was shocked. I was not. But my first thought was to make sure my family back home was safe, as well as my staff in Washington and in the district. Because the sad fact is, the death threats come almost immediately.
It was, of course, personal to me. But the reality is that his response to that video was much bigger than me or any of my colleagues in that video.
When anyone threatens violence against people for engaging in our democracy and our government, they are stifling speech. That is especially true when it's the president accusing someone of treason.
It's dangerous stuff, and I think what I learned in this process is that the American people have had enough of it. Especially as we approach the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence.
I also hope you learned something about me in the process. And that is that I will always stand up for the Constitution, that I will always protect freedom, and I will never back down.

Peter — it’s Pete Buttigieg. We are living through a time in the life of our country when freedom itself is on the line — and few races will test that more directly than Jon Ossoff’s reelection campaign in Georgia. **I’ll share more in a moment. But if you believe, as I do, that hope can be the consequence of action, one meaningful step you can take today is to support Jon’s campaign using this link:** [**https://act.electjon.com/go/Pete**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-jun26.Bh0QdH&refcode=em260625-1-f&utm_campaign=em260625-1-f&t=3&akid=2427%2E5691347%2ERJhwfl) Right now, the same forces working to consolidate total power in Washington have made Jon their top Senate target. And it’s going to take all of us. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]
