Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | Jacob Davis's Market Brief (ads) | | • | Brownstone Research ---|--- | • | StocksToTrade ---|--- | • | Safe Money Report ---|--- | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. Because families like ours are working hard and still falling behind. Because too many politicians have no clue what life is like for the people they represent. Because Congress has too many millionaires, and not nearly enough moms who know how to get things done.

But it also stuck with me, because every child deserves to grow up believing they matter, that they are valued, and that this country has a place for them. I’m proud that every person associated with us on this campaign believes that.

In other words, it was a pretty normal day of joyful chaos for our family. As I watched our kids play and laugh between takes, I was reminded why we're doing this in the first place. Because families like ours are working hard and still falling behind. Because too many politicians have no clue what life is like for the people they represent. Because Congress has too many millionaires, and not nearly enough moms who know how to get things done. That is the chaos of D.C. The kind of chaos that comes when corrupt politicians tear institutions down and leave working families paying the price. Chaos that my 10 years as an SVU Prosecutor have more than prepared me to tackle. At one point during filming, our incredible creative director looked at William and called him a "young king." It made all of us laugh and made Will feel like a million bucks. But it also stuck with me, because every child deserves to grow up believing they matter, that they are valued, and that this country has a place for them. I’m proud that every person associated with us on this campaign believes that. That's the future we're fighting for. If you've already seen the ad, I hope you'll share it with a friend. And if you're able, please consider making a contribution to help us get this message in front of more voters before our June 30 deadline. [] If you have saved your payment information with ActBlue, your donation will go through immediately: DONATE $5 [] DONATE $10 [] DONATE $25 [] DONATE $50 [] DONATE $100 [] OTHER [] Thank you for being part of this campaign and this movement. Warmly, Christina Hines [] Christina is a lifelong advocate for justice and a former prosecutor for survivors of sexual assault, child abuse, and human trafficking. Now she’s running to bring that same dedication to Congress, working to put the middle class first, protect the American Dream, and ensure every community can thrive. She fights for safe neighborhoods, fair opportunities, and a future where everyone can succeed. To learn more about Christina, visit ChristinaHinesForCongress.com [christinahinesforcongress.com] . Breaking News:
**At his most recent rally, Donald Trump announced a gift to the gun industry:_His administration is pushing to pass Concealed Carry Reciprocity._ **
This is the most extreme legislation in years — and reports are saying that the gun lobby could have enough votes to make it into law. But there is still time to fight back.
**[Will you please rush in $10 to help GIFFORDS PAC defeat this NRA-backed bill? GIFFORDS is working to build the largest mobilization program since Donald Trump took office to stop this nationwide concealed carry mandate, but we need your help to combat the GOP’s lies.](https://go.giffords.org/go/65324?c0=giff-em-q22026.lHrQWd&refcode=em260625-1-b&t=1&akid=11582%2E3935704%2ECfZh62)**

This proposal, a concealed carry mandate, would make all of us less safe.
Currently, all 50 states and D.C. have the power to decide and implement their own laws about who can carry loaded, concealed handguns in public. _This bill would allow states with the weakest laws to set the standard for all states._
That means someone from a state with no rules about who can buy or carry weapons could come into your town, neighborhood, or business — and there’s nothing you could do to stop them.
Police leaders across the country have warned that these laws make their jobs nearly Impossible. _But the gun industry doesn’t care...so long as they can sell more guns._
We must fight back to protect our communities.
**GIFFORDS is ready to put as much pressure on lawmakers to vote NO.** That includes running aggressive digital ads, targeting lawmakers in the most important districts, and making sure they know the consequences. All of this will take resources, which is why we need your help.

# _You can’t fake determination_
---
| |
### _Learn about how the fight is more than just the ballot box_
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
Campaigns spend millions of dollars trying to convince voters who a candidate is.Elizabeth Dempsey Beggs doesn't have to. Now I’ve met her, worked beside her, and learned from her. And one thing I’m sure about is that I’ll be there, at the polls, to support her on **August 4**.
Because no consultant, ad, or speech can manufacture what she's doing right now. She's running all 480 miles of Virginia's First District; day after day, town after town mile after mile.
The truth is that anyone can talk about grit. Anyone can claim they're willing to fight for working families. Anyone can promise they'll show up when things get difficult.**Very few people can prove it.**
That's what this run is really about.When Elizabeth gets to Congress, she'll face impossible votes, entrenched interests, and a political establishment that tells people how to think. The question isn't whether those challenges will come but rather if we'll send someone tough enough to meet them head-on.
You don't run 480 miles because it's convenient.You don't run 480 miles because a consultant told you to.You run 480 miles because **quitting isn't in your vocabulary**.
That's the kind of representative Virginia deserves.If you're ready to help send that kind of fighter to Washington, chip in $20 today and sponsor the next mile of the journey.

| |
Join our National Community Call on Black Workers on Stuff Costs Too Much. You’ll hear from **Cleveland Mayor Justin Bibb, Quentin James, Founder and President of The Collective PAC, Michael Bland, Executive Director of the Black Men Vote** , and other community leaders.
**Across the country, Black workers and working-class families are bearing the heaviest burden of the cost-of-living crisis.** From skyrocketing rent to higher grocery prices, your hard-earned dollars are being stretched to the breaking point. This isn't just about "affordability" — it is a fight for economic justice.
[But we cannot fight rising costs if our political power is systematically stripped away.](https://us.list-manage.com/jzUMyBdqOSU?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e)
The recent _Callais_ decision by the Supreme Court undermines Black political power and risks a domino effect in state houses, city councils, and local school boards. If we lose our voice at the ballot box, we lose our leverage to fight for our pockets.

How does this happen?
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=2471%2E135344%2EeEa09N)

Look at this.
[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-26.79HKre&refcode=em260623%2F&t=2&akid=2471%2E135344%2EeEa09N)
Saginaw County Michigan - a county Trump won in 2024 by more than 3,000 votes and almost 3%. Now look at this.
[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-26.79HKre&refcode=em260623&t=3&akid=2471%2E135344%2EeEa09N)
Same county - same election - but Elissa Slotkin beat her Republican opponent by just a few votes.
How does that happen?
If you have followed any of Elissa Slotkin's campaigns for House or Senate, you've heard her say that a key objective in each victory has been to "lose better."
That means doing just a little bit better in the heavier Republican-leaning areas of Michigan — losing with 44% of the vote in Holly Township rather than 39% or losing with 30% of the vote in Conway Township rather than 26%.
Or winning in Saginaw County at the time as Trump.
By the end of Elissa's time in the House, she was the only Democrat who had won in a district that went for Romney in 2012, Trump in 2016 and Trump again in 2020. Then she won her Senate race in Michigan at the same time as Trump carried the state.
That's because she campaigns everywhere and takes no vote for granted.
This idea is one of the reasons Elissa is in hot demand to travel the country to campaign for Democrats who need to "lose better" in order to win their races.
And Elissa wants to show up -- everywhere -- and take no vote for granted. But she needs the resources to get it done.

It’s all because of you.
The momentum we’re seeing right now – from a new poll showing us leading in this race to _The Cook Political Report_ and _Sabato’s Crystal Ball_ shifting Ohio to a Toss Up – is thanks to your grassroots support.
It didn’t happen because a billionaire wrote a big check.
**It happened because you made the critical decision to join this team and engage with our campaign. That matters, and I’m so grateful.**
But today, I’m in a bit of a pickle and could really use your help: _We fell short of yesterday's daily fundraising goal._

__**FROM THE DESK OF MLB LEGEND MARK TEIXEIRA**__

People often say that hitting a baseball is among the hardest things to do in sports.

After nearly two decades in Major League Baseball facing the best pitchers on the planet, I can tell you it certainly isn't easy.

But the truth is, it pales in comparison to the real challenges and rewards of the American Dream: raising a family, building a business, supporting your neighbors, and helping preserve the greatest country the world has ever known.

Those experiences have shaped me far more than any home run, championship, or All-Star appearance ever could.

My name is Mark Teixeira. Many of you know me from my years in Major League Baseball, including my time with the Texas Rangers. But with the help of great American patriots like you, I'm hoping to join President Trump's MAGA majority in Congress.

I had the privilege of playing for what I believe is the greatest franchise in sports, and every time I stepped onto the field, I understood I was representing something bigger than myself.

Today, I'm seeking the opportunity to represent something even greater: the United States of America.

I was fortunate to play for legendary managers who demanded excellence, expected accountability, and never lost sight of winning. President Trump brings that same mentality to leadership: setting high standards, challenging the status quo, and focusing on results.

Just as the Yankees set the standard for excellence in baseball, America has long set the standard for freedom, opportunity, and self-government. Both are built on proud traditions, high expectations, and the belief that every generation has a responsibility to leave things better than they found them.

That's why I'm running.

If you're ready to help bring common-sense conservative leadership and a commitment to service to Congress, I hope you'll stand with me today by making a contribution to our campaign.

Thank you, and God bless America.

Sincerely,

Mark Teixeira

Do this one" [Tell Trump: "If You Think the Reflecting Pool Water Is Clean, Drink It!"](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tfde7ee31-abf2-41b1-bce7-7ab78d99ee8a/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9))_ The Lincoln Memorial's Reflecting Pool is one of the most iconic and photographed sites in America. It was the site of MLK’s “I Have a Dream” speech, countless other gatherings through the years, and millions if not billions of quiet, reflective moments for visitors from throughout the world. **But Donald Trump decided it needed an “extreme makeover”, and not surprisingly, he f***ed it up** [**Add your name, and demand Trump pay for the repairs.**](https://default.salsalabs.org/T365cd61b-47ee-461d-9a62-b27dabd854d5/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) Instead of using actual experts who do this kind of thing, Trump hired a company that had _fixed swimming pools at Mar-a-Lago_ without bothering to get bids from anyone else. The company apparently had no clue what it was doing, and turned the pool into a massive algae orgy — a sea of green muck. Like Jolly Green Giant Chunky Soup. [**It's going to cost a fortune to fix it, and there's no way the rest of us should pay for his stupidity.**](https://default.salsalabs.org/T44596fff-91d2-42f6-92ec-e5c1859e65fb/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) [**Add your name, and demand that Trump pay for the repairs.**](https://default.salsalabs.org/T75f594e1-7fe7-4d26-a351-517fc699882a/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

# Farms, donuts, a parade, and a float down the river. Quite a weekend.

Peter,I have been promising you a little summer fun, and this weekend it finally arrives.

---
|
---
| | **Apple River upstream from the Church Road bridge**
---
| | But before that, today Thursday, June 25th, I’ll be at two farming events: the Farmers Union CD7 Candidate Forum in Star Prairie at 4pm and then the Farm Bureau Meet Up in Clear Lake at 7pm.Then on Friday, I’ll be heading to the heart of the Northwoods to camp overnight for a meetup with the Florence County Dems on Saturday, the 27th, at the pavilion outside the Florence Community Center from 11:30 am to 1 pm. There will be free coffee and donuts, good company, and a whole lot of conversation before the town's Semiquincentennial Parade kicks off. Word on the street is I might bring the guitar along and get folks singing. Consider yourself warned. :-)Then Sunday, the 28th, is the one I have been itching to tell you about. We are grabbing our tubes and some cold beverages to float down the river together, because there is no better way to spend a summer afternoon in this state and no better reminder of exactly what we are fighting to protect.
---
| [Event Details](https://us.list-manage.com/erOwCgEnRO3?e=0c0d11993f&c2id=6a676d78c90e8a1f5821c8d4ac39abd8)
---
| | Our rivers and lakes are the lifeblood of this district, and keeping them clean for the folks who come after us is not negotiable.
Come float, come laugh, come talk about why this stuff matters.
I promise you it beats a stuffy fundraiser any day of the week.
If you want to pitch in and keep this whole operation afloat (pun absolutely intended) you can chip in right here.

Thanks, Chris ~:|

name: Dave Beckwith for Congress
subject: I want you to keep more of your own money
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Dave Beckwith For Congress_
body:
Buy that home. Pay off that debt. You, not Washington, get to make the call.
| | | | [](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress._gg/s1t1b6218b8)
---
| | Hi Friend,
The median home price in Northern Virginia is $725,000. Young professionals and working families are not locked out of the housing market because they do not work hard enough. They are locked out because Washington keeps taking more of their money and handing it back in the form of programs that promise help and deliver disappointment.
**That is why I am proposing a 5% flat income tax rate for every American earning under $200,000.** Not another government program. Not another waiting list. Just more of your own money, back in your hands, to use the way you decide.
---
| | _****_**_If you believe hardworking Northern Virginia families deserve to keep more of what they earn, I am asking for your support today._**_****_
---
[DONATE TO DAVE](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress._gg/s7g804ff6c0)
| | | Washington's answer to the affordability crisis has always been the same: more spending, more bureaucracy, more programs. The result? A median home price of $725,000 in this region, a generation of young people who cannot buy their first home, and student debt that follows families for decades.
These programs do not solve the problem, they consume the resources that could have. The federal government takes your money, runs it through an administrative machine, and delivers back a fraction of it, with strings attached and a waiting list.
Under my plan, a family earning less than $200,000 a year will be able to keep thousands of additional dollars they can direct toward a down payment or a student loan balance, not toward a government program designed to help them do exactly that. I trust the people of Northern Virginia to know what to do with their own money. It is time Washington did too.
The families of this district do not need Washington to spend money on their behalf. They need Washington to stop taking so much of it.
Your support gives this campaign the power to take that fight to Congress.
---
| | |
---
__**_If you are ready to fight for a Northern Virginia every family can afford, please donate to our campaign today.
_**__
[DONATE TO DAVE](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress._gg/sau49c546c1)
|
---
| | Your support has built this campaign from the ground up, and I am grateful for every one of you standing with me.

Let's finish strong.
God Bless, Dave Beckwith
**Beckwith for Congress** _Safe. Strong. Responsible._

This card has by far one of the longest intro APR periods we've seen. Powerful earthquakes strike Venezuela likely killing thousands - Trump says he 's ready to help Two massive earthquakes in rapid succession, a magnitude 7.2 followed 39 seconds later by a 7.5, centered roughly 100 miles west of Caracas. The USGS warned casualties could reach anywhere from 10,000 to 100,000. As of early Thursday, acting President Delcy Rodriguez confirmed at least 164 deaths and nearly 1,000 injuries, with rescue workers still combing through collapsed buildings. The quakes struck during a national holiday, catching many Venezuelans at home. Harrowing footage showed ceiling panels collapsing at Caracas's international airport, baseball stadiums shaking, and residents trapped in rubble. A brief tsunami warning was issued for Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands before being lifted roughly an hour later. President Trump offered full US assistance, pledging to mobilize federal agencies for relief efforts. Venezuela's acting government thanked Washington for its immediate outreach -- a notable diplomatic moment given the two countries' recent fraught history. Louisiana pastor beats the breaks off man who allegedly threatened his family Tony Spell, 48, pastor of Life Tabernacle Church in Baton Rouge, after crossing a four-lane road and attacking his neighbor's 20-year-old son. Spell claims he acted after the neighbor allegedly threatened to rape his wife and grandchildren and kill his family while he was away. He faces up to eight years in prison and is due in court September 15. Video obtained by local outlet WBRZ shows Spell striking the victim dozens of times and wrestling him to the ground, leaving him needing five stitches. Spell later addressed his congregation, comparing the incident to "domestic terrorism" and citing a Bible verse about laying hands on the sick. Spell has a lengthy history of confrontation. He feuded with the same neighbor since at least 2020, was ticketed during the pandemic for holding in-person services, and was previously arrested, though never charged, for an alleged assault outside his church. Trump alleged suspects used sharp blades to slash the new lining, poured corrosive chemicals into the water, and damaged surrounding grass with acid. Multiple arrests and citations have already been made. Trump attributed the damage to "Trump Derangement Syndrome" and called for lengthy prison sentences. Peter, **That’s Becca.** Before the speeches. Before the campaigns. Before she became the first woman ever elected to represent Vermont in Congress. **Back then, Becca was simply a kid trying to understand who she was—and where she belonged. She couldn’t have known she would lead the Vermont Senate. And she certainly couldn’t have known that one day, Vermonters would send her to Congress to make history as the first woman ever elected to serve from the state. # _Our Weekly Newsletter Is Here!_
---
| |
**Hello Everyone!****It was another wonderful week on the campaign trail! Elizabeth and her team enjoyed so many opportunities to connect with communities and voters across the district.****On Saturday, Elizabeth was honored to join the Williamsburg community for a Juneteenth celebration, reflecting on our nation's history and the ongoing work to build a more just future. She also enjoyed spending time with Middle Peninsula Democrats over ice cream, sharing conversations about the issues that matter most to families and communities throughout the region.****A very busy Saturday continued with a summer social hosted by the Henrico Democrats and a joyful Pride celebration at The Bookshelf On Church, where Elizabeth was excited to celebrate Pride with friends and the community.****On Tuesday, Elizabeth also participated in the Influential Women’s Panel, joining incredible voices from advocacy, media, and public service for a great evening of conversation. Special shoutout to all the other panelists: Amanda Nelson of Amanda’s Mild Takes, public servant and Army veteran Sue Fulton, and the owner of the beloved Bookshelf on Church’s, Lisa McLaughlin. ****On Wednesday, Elizabeth was honored to take part in a Congressional Roundtable, hosted by the Congressional Service Women and Women Veterans Caucus, commemorating the 50th anniversary of the first class of women graduating from West Point. With other advocates, Elizabeth honored the trailblazers who opened doors for generations of women like herself to follow.****Thank you to everyone who joined us this week! We look forward to seeing you again soon.**
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
**Upcoming Events:****There are so many events you can join us at this week! Starting on Thursday afternoon, join one of our recurring phonebanks from 6:45-8:00pm ET. After that, Friday is a great day to get out and vote! The weather looks nice, and early voting is open!****This weekend, Elizabeth will be attending a candidate forum in Henrico on Saturday morning. Following, she is thrilled to be celebrating democratic organizing at the VA Dems Blue Commonwealth Gala. This is a great opportunity to join us! Sign up**[**here**](https://us.list-manage.com/fqBiYKbJOs4?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)**, wear a pin, and say hi! Afterwards, Elizabeth will also be attending the Young Dems after party.****On Sunday, Elizabeth is joining the**[**Rural Dems Bluegrass Brunch**](https://us.list-manage.com/15bLMMGtedh?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)**! Stop by for good conversation and good food. Afterwards, join us for a**[**virtual phonebank**](https://us.list-manage.com/jedlKVSmC8Q?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)**at 2pm, or stop by the Henrico County Democratic Committee’s candidate forum!****On Monday, Elizabeth will join two other Democratic candidates for a**[**Veterans Candidate forum**](https://us.list-manage.com/lg4mHvGWmU9?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)[**.**](https://us.list-manage.com/7SS6JvnljeD?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)**Join us and hear her take on serving her country - both in and out of the military.****Have a great week, Virginia!**
---

It's worth noting that the state auditor is the only statewide elected Republican, with Democrats winning the 2024 races for governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general, and secretary of state.
Now, among massive protests from young voters, the MAGA-fied North Carolina State Elections Board recently shot down proposals to continue having early voting sites at several universities around the state . These weren't new sites either; these were places where North Carolina had provided early voting locations for a decade or more.
This is voter suppression, plain and simple, by making it harder for eligible, registered voters to vote in-person by taking away their polling place. It's another demonstration of how opponents of voting rights in North Carolina are more focused on expanding and cementing their own power than they are in serving the people and having fair elections.

_U.S.-Iran technical talks[ set](https://substack.com/redirect/b7279ceb-87d8-43b4-a1fe-ec50ad45c24b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to resume next week, Pakistan says. Iran [says](https://substack.com/redirect/7025279c-0338-4c65-b0eb-9453c8aaedc7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) no nuclear inspections until final deal reached. Iranian official [challenges](https://substack.com/redirect/9594f79e-18aa-47e8-ae05-63396930a490?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio on path to regional peace. Rubio rejects fees in Strait of Hormuz. Gulf leaders [meet](https://substack.com/redirect/e39aaf73-3e4e-4718-a1a2-e570f1138b19?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to negotiate Strait of Hormuz. IRGC [calls](https://substack.com/redirect/d5c0c069-65bb-4580-9d3f-34d4a7d638de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Hormuz shipping lane "unacceptable." Oil prices [fall](https://substack.com/redirect/47637bf4-8946-44ee-b689-045ab5ce9521?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to pre-Iran war levels as shipping rebounds. President Donald Trump [says](https://substack.com/redirect/a8a42a67-11b3-4f39-b017-eb14628b9098?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) responsibility for Minab school attack may "never be determined." Israel [kills](https://substack.com/redirect/10691f54-988b-4f73-a077-d56ff40dfb16?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) three, burns houses despite "ceasefire" in Lebanon. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu [says](https://substack.com/redirect/be8d23cd-4408-4e19-bcf3-1563ab18d6da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Israel will maintain southern Lebanon "security zone" as long as he is prime minister. Israel [floods](https://substack.com/redirect/88fad6b4-bf5d-4fcf-9bd5-f935d76d1236?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) streets in Al-Maghazi camp with cement. Israeli forces [kill](https://substack.com/redirect/b88d37b8-b2ff-43f6-92ff-3b5899a078bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two Palestinians during West Bank raids. Israel [seizes](https://substack.com/redirect/3d8e3c36-c3a7-46ba-908c-c04139d9b954?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 115 acres of Palestinian land to expand settlement bloc. Trump [cancels](https://substack.com/redirect/4f63dc94-6186-4897-a2e4-1c416d4a3d7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) housing bill signing, demands SAVE America Act pass first. White House [requests](https://substack.com/redirect/d69eeeac-900d-4ba4-ade9-376a36c9aab0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) $87.6 billion in supplemental funding. Second Iran War Powers resolution [fails](https://substack.com/redirect/ff289bed-716d-4638-bde0-cf950c33ff20?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Federal judge [scraps](https://substack.com/redirect/f965cfa2-fc10-4ba2-a96a-854e39aa31dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) most of Trump executive order on elections. Three ICC judges [sue](https://substack.com/redirect/3befe3ea-69a7-4455-9715-028a609d27dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Trump administration over sanctions. At least 164 [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/9ef8daab-242c-4935-80b3-31d4bbdbe2be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in pair of major earthquakes in Venezuela. Rubio [says](https://substack.com/redirect/b0367443-ccf1-4437-b71f-7da9541a0bee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) U.S. pressing for ceasefire in Sudan. Left-wing candidate Ivan Cepeda [concedes](https://substack.com/redirect/6034af90-1c9b-48de-bb6e-b930b87b9824?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Colombia. App workers in Mexico stage two-hour strike [demanding](https://substack.com/redirect/e7048a3a-d1ea-480f-9331-494e2ef3144e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) fair pay and labor protections. North Korean soldier [defects](https://substack.com/redirect/0a17e707-aa90-4d7f-88c2-bd08c6d8689c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) across heavily fortified border. Iraq [threatens](https://substack.com/redirect/09c151f9-a76f-4f6f-bf0b-102cfad49d7c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to leave OPEC as oil revenues collapse. Ukrainian drone strike [knocks](https://substack.com/redirect/14ca698a-9bfe-4fbe-a844-351048a98d54?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) out power in Sevastopol._

# Iran and Ceasefire
* **U.S.-Iran technical talks set to resume next week, Pakistan says:** Technical talks between the United States and Iran will [resume](https://substack.com/redirect/b7279ceb-87d8-43b4-a1fe-ec50ad45c24b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) next week, most likely on Tuesday, Pakistani Foreign Ministry spokesman Tahir Andrabi reportedly said on Wednesday, according to AFP.
* Pakistan and Qatar are mediating the talks under the Islamabad memorandum of understanding signed June 17. The first round of negotiations was held this week in Lucerne, Switzerland.
* **Iran says no nuclear inspections until final deal reached:** Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi [rejected](https://substack.com/redirect/7025279c-0338-4c65-b0eb-9453c8aaedc7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the UN nuclear watchdog's claim that inspections of Iranian sites are imminent on Wednesday, saying on X that no meeting took place with IAEA chief Rafael Grossi during last week's talks in Switzerland, and that there is no plan to grant access to facilities struck during the war or to Iran's nuclear material until a final agreement and full sanctions relief.

* **Iranian official challenges Rubio on path to regional peace:** Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei [hit back](https://substack.com/redirect/9594f79e-18aa-47e8-ae05-63396930a490?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who claimed there could be no end to regional hostilities "as long as Iranian proxies are launching missiles and drones from Iraq." "No one will be fooled," Baghaei wrote. "We can't have a peaceful region so long as American militarism and interventionism persist, and their occupying proxy [Israel] continues, with absolute impunity, to inflict endless wars across the region and perpetrate genocide, terror, violence, and every [type of] atrocity."

* **Rubio rejects fees in Strait of Hormuz:** U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Thursday said that Iran would not be permitted to impose tolls or transit fees on vessels using the Strait of Hormuz under any final agreement with Washington. Speaking during a regional tour in the United Arab Emirates and later at a Gulf Cooperation Council meeting in Bahrain, Rubio said, "There is zero support from Gulf countries for tolls or fees on the Strait of Hormuz," adding, "It's an international waterway. No country is allowed to charge tolls or fees on an international waterway." He warned that allowing countries to charge for passage because a waterway borders their territory would create "total chaos," adding that such a precedent would spread "throughout the world like a contagion."
* Iran's chief negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said Monday that "Hormuz will never return" to its pre-war state, with Oman and Iran releasing a statement on Wednesday saying they will negotiate the future arrangements and costs of services associated with the strategic waterway.
* **Gulf leaders meet to negotiate Hormuz:** Qatar's prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, [met](https://substack.com/redirect/e39aaf73-3e4e-4718-a1a2-e570f1138b19?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Oman's ruler in Muscat on Wednesday to launch a new negotiating track between Iran, Iraq, and Gulf Arab states over the Strait of Hormuz's future management, a diplomat briefed on the talks told Reuters.
* The discussions, separate from the U.S.-Iran negotiations, carry out a provision of the memorandum of understanding calling for Iran to coordinate with Oman, Iraq, and other Gulf states on navigation and maritime services, with Pakistan as proposed mediator.
* Gulf states are expected to push for no transit fees, while Iran is likely to propose environmental, navigation, and security charges, with toll-free passage under the U.S. deal set to last only 60 days.
* Separate reconciliation talks are reportedly [planned](https://substack.com/redirect/2252faa7-e20c-45dc-a8ae-1e1d4a20310b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to take place in Saudi Arabia, Reuters reported, aimed at mending ties between Iran and the Gulf States.
* **IRGC calls Hormuz shipping lane "unacceptable": **Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) [warned](https://substack.com/redirect/d5c0c069-65bb-4580-9d3f-34d4a7d638de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a statement on Wednesday that a newly announced shipping lane is "unacceptable" and "completely dangerous." Oman and the UN-affiliated International Maritime Organization had announced a southern temporary shipping corridor to allow hundreds of ships and roughly 11,000 stranded seafarers to transit the Strait of Hormuz the previous day.
* In its statement, the IRGC argued that safe passage is only possible via routes approved by Iran, and insisted that all vessels must coordinate with its navy via international maritime Channel 16 when transiting the strait. "Navigation outside these routes is extremely dangerous and prohibited, and we warn all vessels to strictly refrain from any transit outside the designated routes," it said.

* **Oil prices fall to pre-Iran war levels as shipping rebounds:** Brent crude [fell](https://substack.com/redirect/47637bf4-8946-44ee-b689-045ab5ce9521?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to $72.24 a barrel on Thursday, returning to pre-Iran war levels and marking a decline of more than 20% this month, The Guardian reported, as vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz doubled over the previous 24 hours to its highest level since late February, according to CNN and MarineTraffic data.
* **Trump says responsibility for Minab school attack may "never be determined": **Trump [said](https://substack.com/redirect/a8a42a67-11b3-4f39-b017-eb14628b9098?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) he had not seen the report into the Minab school attack--which killed at least 165, mostly children--when asked about the matter in the Oval Office on Wednesday, telling a reporter he had to "wait for it to be complete," and casting doubt on the possibility of determining the responsibility of any party. "I don't know that they're ever going to solve that problem. I don't know that they're ever going to say it was one of our missiles."
* He called the attack "horrible," though he indicated it was unlikely the U.S. was at fault because "missiles were flying all over the place."
* Nearly every investigation of the attack has found the United States [culpable](https://substack.com/redirect/62af3314-4c7f-4d62-a156-93a641893054?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), including preliminary investigations from the U.S. military itself.
* **Iran 's lead negotiator calls MOU "America's declaration of defeat": **Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran's lead negotiator and Speaker of Parliament, [said](https://substack.com/redirect/786a57b3-6f01-46dc-b7a0-7ed07eb72d6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at a conference in Baku, Azerbaijan on Wednesday that the memorandum of understanding to end the war represents "America's declaration of defeat." "The Islamabad understanding was not the result of pressure and coercion, but rather the result of the resistance and authority of the brave Iranian nation," Ghalibaf said.
* In the same speech, Ghalibaf also noted that the eventual withdrawal of foreign military forces from the region--where the U.S. maintains multiple bases--was a "strategic goal" for Iran.

* **Israel kills three, burns houses despite "ceasefire":** Three people were [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/10691f54-988b-4f73-a077-d56ff40dfb16?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and one injured after an Israeli drone struck a vehicle traveling on the road between Zawtar and Mefdoun in southern Lebanon's Nabatieh governorate, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Israeli forces also [burned](https://substack.com/redirect/149fd197-03c9-4499-ad8b-bc5eae16e9c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) several homes in the southern Lebanese town of Ain Arab on Thursday after forcibly displacing the residents the previous day, despite residents having only returned after roads to the village were reopened. Separately, Israeli soldiers [released](https://substack.com/redirect/44e58b4f-82b8-496f-af38-412a39dfe3bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Syrian shepherd who had been abducted during an Israeli ground incursion near Al-Mari two days earlier.
* **Netanyahu says Israel will maintain southern Lebanon "security zone" as long as he is prime minister: **Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu [said](https://substack.com/redirect/be8d23cd-4408-4e19-bcf3-1563ab18d6da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday Israel will not withdraw from the "security zone" it occupies in southern Lebanon as long as he remains in office, according to Haaretz, and described overcoming fear as Israel's "greatest achievement" of the war while pledging to address Hezbollah's explosive drones.
* He also said Israel now controls nearly 70 percent of the Gaza Strip and is "suffocating Hamas," recalling earlier pressure he faced not to advance into Rafah in the south of Gaza after the October 7 attacks.
* Israeli military sources on Thursday [denied](https://substack.com/redirect/08d4ff66-383a-40d4-b565-74571fa84803?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reports that Israeli forces had withdrawn from part of the self-declared "buffer zone" in southern Lebanon, contradicting comments by a U.S. State Department official who told Reuters that Israel had pulled back from part of the area as a "significant demonstration of good faith" toward the Lebanese government. A senior Lebanese security official also said authorities were unaware of any Israeli pullback.
* This comes amid the fifth round of U.S.-mediated Israel-Lebanon talks in Washington, with a senior Lebanese security official telling Reuters that military officials will discuss withdrawal and that any concrete plan would emerge only after the talks conclude on Thursday.

# Palestine
* **Killed and wounded:** Over the last 24 hours, two Palestinians were killed and 15 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,043 killed, with 173,417 injured, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.
* Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,031 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,309, while 785 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble.

* **Israel floods streets in Al-Maghazi camp with cement:** Residents of eastern Al-Maghazi camp in central Gaza [told](https://substack.com/redirect/88fad6b4-bf5d-4fcf-9bd5-f935d76d1236?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Drop Site's Mohamed Ahmed that Israeli forces pumped a thick cement-like substance into their neighborhood after tanks advanced near Hosni Al-Masadar Mosque on Sunday, leaving streets buried under hardened concrete and trapping families inside their homes.
* Speaking to journalist Mohamed Ahmed, a resident told Mohamed that people in the area could no longer reach work, evacuate, or transport wheelchair users to medical appointments. "We escaped the siege of gunfire, only to be under the siege of cement," he said.
* Another resident said children and elderly residents had fallen trying to cross the cement-covered roads. He warned the material had seeped into homes and could clog drainage systems. "This is the first time in the history of the Gaza Strip that we are drowning in cement," he said.

* **Israeli forces kill two Palestinians during West Bank raids:** Israeli forces killed two Palestinian men during raids in the occupied West Bank between Wednesday and Thursday morning, Mohammad Zayed from Jenin and Mustafa Al-Khatib from Salfit, according to WAFA. Israeli forces surrounded a house in the town of Al-Yamun, west of Jenin, before fatally shooting Zayed and withholding his body, while Al-Khatib was shot dead during a raid on his home in Salfit, with soldiers leaving his body inside the house. The Palestinian Prisoners' Society [condemned](https://substack.com/redirect/b88d37b8-b2ff-43f6-92ff-3b5899a078bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the killing of the two men, and said the killings reflect "Israel's systematic policy of extrajudicial executions," which it says has escalated since the start of the war on Gaza, and renewed calls for the international community and the United Nations to hold Israeli leaders accountable for unlawful killings.
* **Israel seizes 115 acres of Palestinian land to expand settlement bloc:** Israeli authorities [seized](https://substack.com/redirect/3d8e3c36-c3a7-46ba-908c-c04139d9b954?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 464.4 dunams (114.8 acres) of Palestinian land in the town of Sinjil, north of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, by declaring it "state land," according to WAFA. The Palestinian Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission said the declaration covers the entire area of the Givat Harel settlement outpost, established in 1998 and designated by the Israeli government in December 2025 as a standalone settlement. The land seizure links the settlements of Shilo and Ma'ale Levona along Route 60, creating a continuous settlement corridor that consolidates Israeli control over a wider stretch of Palestinian land in the area.
* **GSF members return from Libyan detention:** Ten members of the Global Sumud Flotilla Land Convoy delegation [arrived](https://substack.com/redirect/0d4ffa9b-4945-441e-935f-ac478866b27f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at Tunis-Carthage International Airport on Tuesday after being detained for 30 days in eastern Libya.
* The activists from nine countries were arrested on May 24 near Sirte while trying to reach Gaza via Egypt's Rafah crossing. They attempted to bring humanitarian aid, including ambulances, medical supplies and equipment, and construction materials, into the Strip before their detention in Eastern Libya.

_By Julian Andreone, with Ryan Grim. Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email Andreone at[ Julian@dropsitenews.com](https://substack.com/redirect/fdacb7d8-51ee-4019-9f49-378d5cea67ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)._
* **Trump cancels housing bill signing, demands SAVE America Act pass first:** President Donald Trump [cancelled](https://substack.com/redirect/4f63dc94-6186-4897-a2e4-1c416d4a3d7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday's planned signing of a bipartisan housing bill, posting on Truth Social that the ceremony was "hereby cancelled" until Congress passes the SAVE America Act, an unrelated bill that would require voters to prove U.S. citizenship.
* House Speaker **Mike Johnson** said Trump still plans to sign the housing measure within his 10-day constitutional window, and the bill--which passed 358-32 in the House and 85-5 in the Senate--would become law without his signature if that window lapses.
* Senate Majority Leader **John Thune** said Republicans still lack the votes to pass the SAVE America Act or eliminate the filibuster blocking it.
* **White House requests $87.6 billion in supplemental funding:** The White House [asked](https://substack.com/redirect/d69eeeac-900d-4ba4-ade9-376a36c9aab0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Congress on Wednesday for $87.6 billion in supplemental funding, including $67 billion for the War Department, $1.4 billion for Ebola response, and $11.1 billion in farm assistance, according to a letter from Office of Management and Budget Director **Russell Vought**.
* The Pentagon request is down from the $200 billion War Secretary **Pete Hegseth** had floated in March, but Democratic senators, including **Chris Murphy** and **Mazie Hirono,** said the package seems designed to fail given the party's opposition to providing additional funding for the Iran war.
* **Second Iran War Powers resolution fails:** The Senate [voted](https://substack.com/redirect/ff289bed-716d-4638-bde0-cf950c33ff20?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 50-47 late Wednesday to reject a procedural motion that would have advanced Sen. **Tim Kaine 's** resolution directing President Donald Trump to remove U.S. forces from hostilities against Iran, unless the action was authorized by Congress.
* Republican Sens. **Susan Collins**(Me.) and **Lisa Murkowski** (Alaska) joined most Democrats in voting to advance the measure, while **Rand Paul** (Ky.) voted present after saying on X that he wanted to give Trump "more space and leverage to negotiate" with Iran.
* Sen. **Bill Cassidy**(La.)--who had voted for a separate House-passed war powers resolution a day earlier--voted against advancement after being briefed on Iran at the White House by Vice President **JD Vance** and special envoy **Steve Witkoff**. His vote follows a heated [exchange](https://substack.com/redirect/90625966-2bfa-494d-9e0b-f92a1c34cc52?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with President Donald Trump during a closed-door Senate GOP conference meeting on Wednesday.
* **Federal judge scraps most of Trump executive order on elections** : U.S. District Court Judge **Denise Casper** in Boston permanently [blocked](https://substack.com/redirect/f965cfa2-fc10-4ba2-a96a-854e39aa31dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) most of President Donald Trump's first executive order on elections Wednesday, converting a preliminary injunction issued a year ago into a permanent ban.
* Casper ruled the order--which sought documentary proof of citizenship for voter registration and would have disqualified late-arriving mail ballots, threatening to withhold federal grants from noncompliant states--violated the Constitution's separation of powers, which delegates authority over elections to the states and Congress, not the president. The administration is expected to appeal the decision.
* **Three ICC judges sue Trump administration over sanctions:** Three International Criminal Court judges--**Kimberly Pros** t of Canada, **Reine Alapini-Gansou** of Benin, and **Solomy Balungi Bossa** of Uganda--[filed suit](https://substack.com/redirect/3befe3ea-69a7-4455-9715-028a609d27dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the Southern District of New York on Wednesday, arguing that sanctions imposed against them by the Trump administration exceeded the president's legal authority.
* The judges claim the sanctions, imposed over the past year in response to ICC investigations into Israeli and American conduct and arrest warrants against Israeli leaders, were not based on a genuine national emergency as required under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act. "Being subjected to such sanctions under IEEPA is tantamount to the financial death penalty. Due to the sanctions, Judges Prost, Bossa, and Alapini-Gansou are no longer able, among other things, to use credit cards; access banking services; use common online platforms, such as Amazon and Google; book travel; and in some cases, obtain health insurance," the lawsuit said.
* **Mamdani defends boosting primary challengers:** New York City Mayor **Zohran Mamdani** [defended](https://substack.com/redirect/a3e40b5c-0d76-44d4-aa33-07afbb3d735a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) endorsing challengers against incumbent Democrats in a television appearance on Wednesday, after New York Attorney General **Letitia James** criticized the move. "All of us are a little frustrated with the Democratic Party. But you don't blow it up," James [told CNN](https://substack.com/redirect/a4b6d3f8-412d-4c6c-b912-186660c82f46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). "That's what MAGA has done." Mamdani responded that "the Democratic Party is its voters," and New Yorkers are backing "a new kind of politics" centered on the working class. He said he kept his promise to voters to use every tool, including his political capital, to help elect candidates who would advance the same agenda in Albany and Congress.
* **Federal judge dismisses DOJ lawsuit against four New Jersey "sanctuary" cities: **A federal judge [dismissed](https://substack.com/redirect/d2b63175-81b2-4c80-9b26-a0fcf337b5d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Justice Department lawsuit against Newark, Jersey City, Hoboken, and Paterson on Wednesday that had accused the cities of shielding undocumented immigrants from federal immigration enforcement.
* Judge **Evelyn Padin** ruled the suit failed to account for New Jersey's 2008 immigrant trust directive, which governs how local police interact with federal immigration authorities, meaning the federal government lacked standing.

# Other International News
* **At least 164 killed in pair of major earthquakes in Venezuela:** At least 164 people were [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/9ef8daab-242c-4935-80b3-31d4bbdbe2be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and roughly 971 injured by two powerful earthquakes that struck Venezuela Wednesday evening, Acting President Delcy Rodriguez said early Thursday, with the toll expected to rise as rescuers continue searching collapsed buildings.

* The coastal state of La Guaira was hit hardest, according to Rodriguez, who declared a state of emergency and said the quakes forced the closure of Caracas's main international airport.
* President Donald Trump said he had directed U.S. agencies to mobilize aid, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio said search teams, medical resources, and humanitarian assistance were being deployed to Venezuela, with additional offers of help coming from Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, China, Ecuador, El Salvador, Mexico, Panama, and Uruguay.

Iraq's oil-dependent budget has been badly hit by the Iran war and the disruption of exports through the Strait of Hormuz, increasing pressure on Baghdad to push for a higher output ceiling as OPEC reviews members' production capacity for future quota baselines. The reported threat comes amid the recent departure of the UAE from the group, which works with members to manage global oil supply and prices.
* **Ukrainian drone strike knocks out power in Sevastopol:** A Ukrainian drone [attack](https://substack.com/redirect/14ca698a-9bfe-4fbe-a844-351048a98d54?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Russian-occupied Crimea hit Sevastopol's main power substation overnight, cutting electricity in parts of the strategically important port city, according to Ukrainian officials and the Moscow-installed governor. The strike comes as Kyiv has escalated attacks on Russian-held energy and logistics infrastructure, including facilities tied to fuel supplies and military operations in Crimea, leading to reported gas shortages in the territory which was taken by Russia in 2014.

Drop Site Daily: June 25, 2026 | | | Jun 25 | | | | | | | | | | | | U.S.-Iran technical talks to resume next week, Pakistan says. Iran no nuclear inspections until final deal reached. Iran and Ceasefire U.S.-Iran technical talks set to resume next week, Pakistan says: Technical talks between the United States and Iran will next week, most likely on Tuesday, Pakistani Foreign Ministry spokesman Tahir Andrabi reportedly said on Wednesday, according to AFP. Pakistan and Qatar are mediating the talks under the Islamabad memorandum of understanding signed June 17. The first round of negotiations was held this week in Lucerne, Switzerland. Iran says no nuclear inspections until final deal reached: Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi the UN nuclear watchdog's claim that inspections of Iranian sites are imminent on Wednesday, saying on X that no meeting took place with IAEA chief Rafael Grossi during last week's talks in Switzerland, and that there is no plan to grant access to facilities struck during the war or to Iran's nuclear material until a final agreement and full sanctions relief. Grossi had said hours earlier that inspections were "going to happen" within days, citing the deal's text placing Iran's nuclear material under IAEA supervision. Iranian official challenges Rubio on path to regional peace: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei at U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who claimed there could be no end to regional hostilities "as long as Iranian proxies are launching missiles and drones from Iraq." "No one will be fooled," Baghaei wrote. "We can't have a peaceful region so long as American militarism and interventionism persist, and their occupying proxy [Israel] continues, with absolute impunity, to inflict endless wars across the region and perpetrate genocide, terror, violence, and every [type of] atrocity." Baghaei added that Washington's "contradictory statements" would only deepen Iranian distrust. Rubio rejects fees in Strait of Hormuz: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Thursday said that Iran would not be permitted to impose tolls or transit fees on vessels using the Strait of Hormuz under any final agreement with Washington. Speaking during a regional tour in the United Arab Emirates and later at a Gulf Cooperation Council meeting in Bahrain, Rubio said, "There is zero support from Gulf countries for tolls or fees on the Strait of Hormuz," adding, "It's an international waterway. No country is allowed to charge tolls or fees on an international waterway." He warned that allowing countries to charge for passage because a waterway borders their territory would create "total chaos," adding that such a precedent would spread "throughout the world like a contagion." Iran's chief negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said Monday that "Hormuz will never return" to its pre-war state, with Oman and Iran releasing a statement on Wednesday saying they will negotiate the future arrangements and costs of services associated with the strategic waterway. Gulf leaders meet to negotiate Hormuz: Qatar's prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, Oman's ruler in Muscat on Wednesday to launch a new negotiating track between Iran, Iraq, and Gulf Arab states over the Strait of Hormuz's future management, a diplomat briefed on the talks told Reuters. The discussions, separate from the U.S.-Iran negotiations, carry out a provision of the memorandum of understanding calling for Iran to coordinate with Oman, Iraq, and other Gulf states on navigation and maritime services, with Pakistan as proposed mediator. Gulf states are expected to push for no transit fees, while Iran is likely to propose environmental, navigation, and security charges, with toll-free passage under the U.S. deal set to last only 60 days. Separate reconciliation talks are reportedly to take place in Saudi Arabia, Reuters reported, aimed at mending ties between Iran and the Gulf States. IRGC calls Hormuz shipping lane "unacceptable": Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) in a statement on Wednesday that a newly announced shipping lane is "unacceptable" and "completely dangerous." Oman and the UN-affiliated International Maritime Organization had announced a southern temporary shipping corridor to allow hundreds of ships and roughly 11,000 stranded seafarers to transit the Strait of Hormuz the previous day. In its statement, the IRGC argued that safe passage is only possible via routes approved by Iran, and insisted that all vessels must coordinate with its navy via international maritime Channel 16 when transiting the strait. "Navigation outside these routes is extremely dangerous and prohibited, and we warn all vessels to strictly refrain from any transit outside the designated routes," it said. Oil prices fall to pre-Iran war levels as shipping rebounds: Brent crude to $72.24 a barrel on Thursday, returning to pre-Iran war levels and marking a decline of more than 20% this month, The Guardian reported, as vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz doubled over the previous 24 hours to its highest level since late February, according to CNN and MarineTraffic data. Trump says responsibility for Minab school attack may "never be determined": Trump he had not seen the report into the Minab school attack--which killed at least 165, mostly children--when asked about the matter in the Oval Office on Wednesday, telling a reporter he had to "wait for it to be complete," and casting doubt on the possibility of determining the responsibility of any party. "I don't know that they're ever going to solve that problem. I don't know that they're ever going to say it was one of our missiles." He called the attack "horrible," though he indicated it was unlikely the U.S. was at fault because "missiles were flying all over the place." Nearly every investigation of the attack has found the United States , including preliminary investigations from the U.S. military itself. Iran 's lead negotiator calls MOU "America's declaration of defeat": Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran's lead negotiator and Speaker of Parliament, at a conference in Baku, Azerbaijan on Wednesday that the memorandum of understanding to end the war represents "America's declaration of defeat." "The Islamabad understanding was not the result of pressure and coercion, but rather the result of the resistance and authority of the brave Iranian nation," Ghalibaf said. In the same speech, Ghalibaf also noted that the eventual withdrawal of foreign military forces from the region--where the U.S. maintains multiple bases--was a "strategic goal" for Iran. Lebanon Killed and wounded: Lebanon's Health Ministry 19 more people died over the past 24 hours from wounds sustained in previous Israeli attacks, bringing the death toll since hostilities resumed on March 2 to 4,211 killed and 12,173 wounded. Israel kills three, burns houses despite "ceasefire": Three people were and one injured after an Israeli drone struck a vehicle traveling on the road between Zawtar and Mefdoun in southern Lebanon's Nabatieh governorate, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Israeli forces also several homes in the southern Lebanese town of Ain Arab on Thursday after forcibly displacing the residents the previous day, despite residents having only returned after roads to the village were reopened. Separately, Israeli soldiers a Syrian shepherd who had been abducted during an Israeli ground incursion near Al-Mari two days earlier. Netanyahu says Israel will maintain southern Lebanon "security zone" as long as he is prime minister: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday Israel will not withdraw from the "security zone" it occupies in southern Lebanon as long as he remains in office, according to Haaretz, and described overcoming fear as Israel's "greatest achievement" of the war while pledging to address Hezbollah's explosive drones. He also said Israel now controls nearly 70 percent of the Gaza Strip and is "suffocating Hamas," recalling earlier pressure he faced not to advance into Rafah in the south of Gaza after the October 7 attacks. Israeli military sources on Thursday reports that Israeli forces had withdrawn from part of the self-declared "buffer zone" in southern Lebanon, contradicting comments by a U.S. State Department official who told Reuters that Israel had pulled back from part of the area as a "significant demonstration of good faith" toward the Lebanese government. A senior Lebanese security official also said authorities were unaware of any Israeli pullback. This comes amid the fifth round of U.S.-mediated Israel-Lebanon talks in Washington, with a senior Lebanese security official telling Reuters that military officials will discuss withdrawal and that any concrete plan would emerge only after the talks conclude on Thursday. Palestine Killed and wounded: Over the last 24 hours, two Palestinians were killed and 15 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,043 killed, with 173,417 injured, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,031 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,309, while 785 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israel floods streets in Al-Maghazi camp with cement: Residents of eastern Al-Maghazi camp in central Gaza Drop Site's Mohamed Ahmed that Israeli forces pumped a thick cement-like substance into their neighborhood after tanks advanced near Hosni Al-Masadar Mosque on Sunday, leaving streets buried under hardened concrete and trapping families inside their homes. Speaking to journalist Mohamed Ahmed, a resident told Mohamed that people in the area could no longer reach work, evacuate, or transport wheelchair users to medical appointments. "We escaped the siege of gunfire, only to be under the siege of cement," he said. Another resident said children and elderly residents had fallen trying to cross the cement-covered roads. He warned the material had seeped into homes and could clog drainage systems. "This is the first time in the history of the Gaza Strip that we are drowning in cement," he said. Israeli forces kill two Palestinians during West Bank raids: Israeli forces killed two Palestinian men during raids in the occupied West Bank between Wednesday and Thursday morning, Mohammad Zayed from Jenin and Mustafa Al-Khatib from Salfit, according to WAFA. Israeli forces surrounded a house in the town of Al-Yamun, west of Jenin, before fatally shooting Zayed and withholding his body, while Al-Khatib was shot dead during a raid on his home in Salfit, with soldiers leaving his body inside the house. The Palestinian Prisoners' Society the killing of the two men, and said the killings reflect "Israel's systematic policy of extrajudicial executions," which it says has escalated since the start of the war on Gaza, and renewed calls for the international community and the United Nations to hold Israeli leaders accountable for unlawful killings. Israel seizes 115 acres of Palestinian land to expand settlement bloc: Israeli authorities 464.4 dunams (114.8 acres) of Palestinian land in the town of Sinjil, north of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, by declaring it "state land," according to WAFA. The Palestinian Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission said the declaration covers the entire area of the Givat Harel settlement outpost, established in 1998 and designated by the Israeli government in December 2025 as a standalone settlement. The land seizure links the settlements of Shilo and Ma'ale Levona along Route 60, creating a continuous settlement corridor that consolidates Israeli control over a wider stretch of Palestinian land in the area. GSF members return from Libyan detention: Ten members of the Global Sumud Flotilla Land Convoy delegation at Tunis-Carthage International Airport on Tuesday after being detained for 30 days in eastern Libya. The activists from nine countries were arrested on May 24 near Sirte while trying to reach Gaza via Egypt's Rafah crossing. They attempted to bring humanitarian aid, including ambulances, medical supplies and equipment, and construction materials, into the Strip before their detention in Eastern Libya. U.S. News By Julian Andreone, with Ryan Grim. Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email Andreone at. Trump cancels housing bill signing, demands SAVE America Act pass first: President Donald Trump Wednesday's planned signing of a bipartisan housing bill, posting on Truth Social that the ceremony was "hereby cancelled" until Congress passes the SAVE America Act, an unrelated bill that would require voters to prove U.S. citizenship. House Speaker Mike Johnson said Trump still plans to sign the housing measure within his 10-day constitutional window, and the bill--which passed 358-32 in the House and 85-5 in the Senate--would become law without his signature if that window lapses. Senate Majority Leader John Thune said Republicans still lack the votes to pass the SAVE America Act or eliminate the filibuster blocking it. White House requests $87.6 billion in supplemental funding: The White House Congress on Wednesday for $87.6 billion in supplemental funding, including $67 billion for the War Department, $1.4 billion for Ebola response, and $11.1 billion in farm assistance, according to a letter from Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought. The Pentagon request is down from the $200 billion War Secretary Pete Hegseth had floated in March, but Democratic senators, including Chris Murphy and Mazie Hirono, said the package seems designed to fail given the party's opposition to providing additional funding for the Iran war. Second Iran War Powers resolution fails: The Senate 50-47 late Wednesday to reject a procedural motion that would have advanced Sen. Tim Kaine 's resolution directing President Donald Trump to remove U.S. forces from hostilities against Iran, unless the action was authorized by Congress. Republican Sens. Susan Collins(Me.) and Lisa Murkowski (Alaska) joined most Democrats in voting to advance the measure, while Rand Paul (Ky.) voted present after saying on X that he wanted to give Trump "more space and leverage to negotiate" with Iran. Sen. Bill Cassidy(La.)--who had voted for a separate House-passed war powers resolution a day earlier--voted against advancement after being briefed on Iran at the White House by Vice President JD Vance and special envoy Steve Witkoff. His vote follows a heated with President Donald Trump during a closed-door Senate GOP conference meeting on Wednesday. Federal judge scraps most of Trump executive order on elections : U.S. District Court Judge Denise Casper in Boston permanently most of President Donald Trump's first executive order on elections Wednesday, converting a preliminary injunction issued a year ago into a permanent ban. Casper ruled the order--which sought documentary proof of citizenship for voter registration and would have disqualified late-arriving mail ballots, threatening to withhold federal grants from noncompliant states--violated the Constitution's separation of powers, which delegates authority over elections to the states and Congress, not the president. The administration is expected to appeal the decision. Three ICC judges sue Trump administration over sanctions: Three International Criminal Court judges--Kimberly Pros t of Canada, Reine Alapini-Gansou of Benin, and Solomy Balungi Bossa of Uganda-- in the Southern District of New York on Wednesday, arguing that sanctions imposed against them by the Trump administration exceeded the president's legal authority. The judges claim the sanctions, imposed over the past year in response to ICC investigations into Israeli and American conduct and arrest warrants against Israeli leaders, were not based on a genuine national emergency as required under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act. "Being subjected to such sanctions under IEEPA is tantamount to the financial death penalty. Due to the sanctions, Judges Prost, Bossa, and Alapini-Gansou are no longer able, among other things, to use credit cards; access banking services; use common online platforms, such as Amazon and Google; book travel; and in some cases, obtain health insurance," the lawsuit said. Mamdani defends boosting primary challengers: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani endorsing challengers against incumbent Democrats in a television appearance on Wednesday, after New York Attorney General Letitia James criticized the move. "All of us are a little frustrated with the Democratic Party. But you don't blow it up," James . "That's what MAGA has done." Mamdani responded that "the Democratic Party is its voters," and New Yorkers are backing "a new kind of politics" centered on the working class. He said he kept his promise to voters to use every tool, including his political capital, to help elect candidates who would advance the same agenda in Albany and Congress. Federal judge dismisses DOJ lawsuit against four New Jersey "sanctuary" cities: A federal judge a Justice Department lawsuit against Newark, Jersey City, Hoboken, and Paterson on Wednesday that had accused the cities of shielding undocumented immigrants from federal immigration enforcement. Judge Evelyn Padin ruled the suit failed to account for New Jersey's 2008 immigrant trust directive, which governs how local police interact with federal immigration authorities, meaning the federal government lacked standing. Other International News At least 164 killed in pair of major earthquakes in Venezuela: At least 164 people were and roughly 971 injured by two powerful earthquakes that struck Venezuela Wednesday evening, Acting President Delcy Rodriguez said early Thursday, with the toll expected to rise as rescuers continue searching collapsed buildings. The U.S. Geological Survey recorded magnitudes of 7.2 and 7.5 in a "doublet" 39 seconds apart, with its predictive modeling showing a 42 percent chance of at least 10,000 fatalities based on historical averages. The coastal state of La Guaira was hit hardest, according to Rodriguez, who declared a state of emergency and said the quakes forced the closure of Caracas's main international airport. President Donald Trump said he had directed U.S. agencies to mobilize aid, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio said search teams, medical resources, and humanitarian assistance were being deployed to Venezuela, with additional offers of help coming from Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, China, Ecuador, El Salvador, Mexico, Panama, and Uruguay. Rubio says U.S. pressing for ceasefire in Sudan: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio reporters in Kuwait that Washington is pressing regional powers to help secure a ceasefire in Sudan, expand humanitarian access, and lay the groundwork for a lasting peace in the country. Rubio said Sudan remains a focus of every regional meeting and confirmed he would raise the war again with Saudi officials. He said Special Envoy Massad Boulos is engaged daily on the crisis, but did not say whether the U.S. had pressed the UAE to end its documented support for the RSF. Separately on Wednesday, the Sudan Doctors Network reported that more than 215 civilians at Daqrees prison in Nyala, South Darfur, died over the past two months from torture and disease outbreaks. The group cited field sources who attributed the deaths to a lack of healthcare, mistreatment, and spreading epidemics at the facility. The group also raised concern over 31 detainees, including children, transferred from the prison to Nyala Hospital despite reportedly having no medical conditions warranting relocation, and said their current whereabouts remain unknown. Cepeda concedes in Colombia: Leftist candidate Ivan Cepeda officially Colombia's presidential runoff election on Wednesday, formalizing his recognition of far-right businessman Abelardo de la Espriella as the country's next president. "I do so as an act of democratic responsibility. I do so to contribute to coexistence, peace and dialogue among Colombians," Cepeda said. President Gustavo Petro also acknowledged the runoff's outcome and announced he will begin the transition process before de la Espriella takes office on August 7, 2026. As the runner-up, Cepeda is entitled to a seat in the Senate, where he has vowed to lead a "democratic, vigilant, and constructive opposition." Hacked emails reveal the role of Jeffrey Epstein 's Israeli network in Africa: Former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Barak coordinated closely with Jeffrey Epstein on mineral, oil, and gas ventures across Africa after leaving his post as Israel's defense minister in 2013, according to U.S. Justice Department documents and hacked Gmail correspondence reviewed by Drop Site News. The emails show Barak drew on former Mossad chief Danny Yatom's private security firm, which trained a Congolese army special operations unit during the 2012-2013 war against the M23 rebel movement, while Epstein simultaneously worked to connect business associates with Congolese officials over mining, oil, and port investments. The cache also details Epstein's later involvement in sanctions diplomacy around Congo's conflict minerals and Russian aluminum interests tied to Barak's own business network. Read the latest from Murtaza Hussain and Ryan Grim for Drop Site. App workers in Mexico stage two-hour strike demanding fair pay and labor protections: Hundreds of app-based drivers and delivery workers across Mexico City and five states held a two-hour work stoppage on May 15, chanting "We are not partners, we are workers" and demanding fair rates, an end to unjustified account deactivations, and a collective labor agreement with platforms including Uber, Didi, and Rappi, according to the National App Workers Union (UNTA). Workers in at least 15 other countries staged similar stoppages during peak hours. The action follows a 2024 labor law reform under President Claudia Sheinbaum that recognized Mexico's 1.2 million app-based workers as employees, though UNTA says income thresholds and earnings exclusions for costs like gas and maintenance leave only about 10 percent of workers eligible for the resulting benefits. Read more about Mexico's gig worker mobilization from Labor Notes, . North Korean soldier defects across heavily fortified border: A North Korean soldier into South Korea on Tuesday night and was taken into custody after indicating he wanted to defect, according to a statement by the South Korean government. The alleged defection marks the fourth known North Korean crossing into the South since President Lee Jae Myung took office in June 2025, and the second military defection in less than a year. The soldier is currently undergoing South Korea's standard defector screening process which can take up to three months. Iraq threatens to leave OPEC as oil revenues collapse : Iraq will consider leaving OPEC if the oil producers' group does not allow Baghdad to sharply raise its production quota, according to a report by Reuters. Iraq's oil-dependent budget has been badly hit by the Iran war and the disruption of exports through the Strait of Hormuz, increasing pressure on Baghdad to push for a higher output ceiling as OPEC reviews members' production capacity for future quota baselines. The reported threat comes amid the recent departure of the UAE from the group, which works with members to manage global oil supply and prices. The strike comes as Kyiv has escalated attacks on Russian-held energy and logistics infrastructure, including facilities tied to fuel supplies and military operations in Crimea, leading to reported gas shortages in the territory which was taken by Russia in 2014. Congress will be decided six weeks before Election Day.
That's not a prediction. That's a fact.
By the time November arrives, millions of ballots will already be cast — early votes banked during the weeks before Election Day by whichever side worked harder to collect them.

**We're doing it again in 2026 — and we need your help to fund it.**
