We're making sure you saw Kim's email, Peter:

Four years after _Roe v. Wade_ was overturned, the attacks on reproductive freedom haven't stopped—** _but neither has Kim._**

As a doctor and a member of Congress, she's fighting every day to protect a woman's right to make their _own_ healthcare decisions. If you haven't already, read Kim's message, then, [**consider chipping in to help her continue that fight in Congress.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134024269/629849030/463063231?refcode=em26_260625_roekic_fndd_gq_act___SHQ_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260625_roekic_fndd_gq_act___SHQ_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=88c51056-db70-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MTExMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4OGM1MTA1Ni1kYjcwLWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2E1NGJlZDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=U54lOl3Xj1jZUbRVeihBy6NsNmlvWh6N0IYOr3HicJE=)

From: Kim Schrier
Date: Jun 24, 2026
Subject: I still remember the shock and the anger I felt on this day four years ago. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134024270/629849031/463063231?refcode=em26_260625_roekic_fndd_gq_act___SHQ_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260625_roekic_fndd_gq_act___SHQ_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=88c51056-db70-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MTExMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4OGM1MTA1Ni1kYjcwLWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2E1NGJlZDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=U54lOl3Xj1jZUbRVeihBy6NsNmlvWh6N0IYOr3HicJE=) Team,

Four years ago, the Supreme Court overturned _Roe v. Wade._

I still remember the shock, the anger, and the fear so many people felt that day. **But what I remember most is hearing from patients, women, and families who worried about what would happen next.**

Unfortunately, _many of those fears became reality._

Since _Roe_ was overturned, states across the country have passed abortion bans and restrictions that have left women without access to care.

Doctors have been forced to navigate confusing laws instead of focusing on their patients.

Women facing medical emergencies have been denied the care they need.

And politicians have inserted themselves into some of the most personal healthcare decisions a person can make.

As a doctor, I have always believed that healthcare decisions belong between a patient and their physician. Not politicians. Not judges. Not bureaucrats. That belief hasn't changed.

Wade. I still remember the shock, the anger, and the fear so many people felt that day. But what I remember most is hearing from patients, women, and families who worried about what would happen next. Unfortunately, many of those fears became reality. Since Roe was overturned, states across the country have passed abortion bans and restrictions that have left women without access to care. Doctors have been forced to navigate confusing laws instead of focusing on their patients. Women facing medical emergencies have been denied the care they need. And politicians have inserted themselves into some of the most personal healthcare decisions a person can make. As a doctor, I have always believed that healthcare decisions belong between a patient and their physician. Not politicians. Not judges. Not bureaucrats. That belief hasn't changed. In Congress, I've fought to protect reproductive freedom at every opportunity, and I've fought back— and will continue to fight back —against every effort to restrict access to care. I have, and will always, support legislation to safeguard reproductive rights, and speak out against extremist attacks on women's healthcare. And this fight is far from over. After Jon Fetherston and Graham Pollard arrived at a Kennebunk protest, several demonstrators refused to explain their signs while others argued over Trump, the Epstein files and the reflecting pool. The exchanges highlighted the gap between anti-Trump slogans, public protest and the ability of demonstrators to defend their positions on camera.

name: Tom Fitton
subject: 250 years ago, they risked everything
body:
Will you Keep Faith With The Founders — 250 years later?
| [ ](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83702&L=14409&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249TWF5JnV0bV90ZXJtPU5vbi1Eb25vcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=8b1ea2406c2235a7e72abe41770202fd3fe922e3a9843b295763736d5e3f2fd4)
---
**_Keeping Faith with the Founders -- 250 Years Later_** _" A popular Government without popular information, or the means of acquiring it, is but a Prologue to a Farce or a Tragedy, or perhaps both."_ -- James Madison Dear Fellow Patriot On July 4th, the United States of America turns 250 years old. A quarter of a millennium since a handful of brave men put _everything_ on the line -- their lives, their fortunes, their sacred honor -- to give us something the world had never seen. A government that answers to _us_. Not the other way around. And Fellow Patriot, I need to be straight with you about something before the fireworks start... I'm writing because **I'm worried.** **I 'm worried about America.** And what keeps me up at night is this... **... Would the Founders even recognize the government we have today? ** Think about it. Those brave men risked everything -- their lives, their fortunes, their sacred honor -- to give us something special. A government that answers to _us._ Not the other way around. But they warned us. They said we'd have to stay vigilant... that freedom isn't free. Well, my friend, look around at what's happened. **Today we have:**
* A bloated **secretive** bureaucracy

* **Leftist** politicians holding our founding principles in contempt

* A **Deep State** "permanent" government that hates transparency

* Weaponized **lawfare** against **President Trump** and countless innocent Americans

James Madison saw this coming. He warned us that freedom is lost not through revolution -- but "by gradual and silent encroachments by those in power." Gradually. Silently. That's exactly how they've been doing it. **But that 's where we come in.** Since 1994, **Judicial Watch** has helped carry **the Founders '** torch of freedom and justice. For 32 years we've used the courts and the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) to force government transparency, expose corruption, and hold the all-powerful **Deep State** accountable. Because of patriots who believe in our mission, Judicial Watch has become... **... the modern-day Faith Keepers our Founders envisioned.** Over the past 32 years, it's been those patriots who have _[made every fight possible](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83702&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)_.
* Blowing the lid off of the Clinton scandals
* Exposing Obama's IRS targeting conservatives
* Revealing the Biden family's criminality
* Taking on the outrageous lawfare against **President Trump**
* Fighting for clean elections all the way to the **Supreme Court**
* Forcing states to clean up their dirty voter rolls -- nearly **7 million** dirty names removed and counting
* Uncovering billions in government waste, fraud, and corruption
* Leading the national effort to enforce our immigration laws

But here's the thing. We don't work for them. **We work for YOU.** And because we answer only to you, we do it all without a single dime of government money. In fact, we do **MORE** than the federal agencies, **MORE** than Congress, **MORE** than the media to uncover and stop government corruption. **That 's why I'm writing to YOU.** I know you've been following our work and I'm grateful for that. You've seen what we're up against -- and what we're accomplishing. | | On October 21st, I walked onto the floor of the U.S. Senate and started talking. I didn't stop for more than 22 hours. **I was ringing the alarm.** The authoritarian takeover is not down the street or around the corner. It is here now. I outlined the 10 rules of Trump's authoritarian playbook—a playbook followed by strongmen leaders around the world—because it is critical to understand what we're up against. Here's what they are:
1. **Fire the referees** — Purging inspectors general, independent agency leaders, and career DOJ attorneys whose job was to catch corruption and keep government honest.

2. **Pack the government with loyalists** — A rubber-stamp Senate confirming unqualified, dangerous nominees, sometimes more than 100 at once in a single vote.

3. **Demonize an enemy within** — Targeting immigrants with dehumanizing rhetoric while a massively expanded ICE terrorizes communities.

4. **Disregard due process** — Detaining and disappearing people, including U.S. citizens, without ever letting them reach a lawyer.

5. **Silence free speech** — Deporting students for their opinions, while networks settle lawsuits and pull hosts under political pressure.

6. **Steal Congress's power of the purse** — Unilaterally freezing or killing programs Congress already funded, a power the Constitution reserves for Congress alone.

7. **Abuse government authority** — Weaponizing licenses, security clearances, and research funding to pressure law firms, universities, and broadcasters into line.

8. **Weaponize the justice system** — Prosecuting political opponents while pardoning nearly 1,600 January 6th defendants and a convicted drug-trafficking former head of state.

9. **Use the military to suppress dissent** — Federalizing the National Guard and deploying troops into American cities, even after federal courts ruled against it.

10. **Rig the next election** — Consolidating voter files, pushing mid-decade gerrymandering, and working to gut mail-in voting.

Democracies rarely die at the hands of men with guns. They die when elected officials erode the separation of powers, one rule at a time. **But this is reversible. It takes two things: sustained, organized citizen action, and an unmistakable rejection of authoritarianism at the next election.** I laid out the full picture in a short report called Ring the Alarm Bells. It automatically sends legal removal requests to over 420 data brokers and people-search sites, deleting your personal information at the source. https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-em-26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-em-26]
Peter, it’s been almost a year since Republicans strong-armed their disastrous budget bill through Congress and Donald Trump signed it into law.
Since then, millions of Americans have been stripped of their health coverage, and millions of families who relied on SNAP to put food on the table are now going hungry. Working families, small children, seniors, and people with disabilities have been impacted.
This administration, aided by the Republican majorities in Congress, made those cuts to help pay for massive tax breaks for the wealthiest Americans and massive corporations. In total, $1.5 trillion that would have gone toward funding public priorities instead stayed in the pockets of the top 1%.
And now, is anyone at all surprised to see that Elon Musk just became the world’s first trillionaire?
That’s the MAGA agenda: creating trillionaires and kicking millions of Americans off their health insurance, to the point that 1 in 3 Americans currently can’t afford to see a doctor.
We should call it what it is: One of the biggest transfers of wealth from the working class to the richest people in our nation’s history.
Cruelty. Greed.
And above all, a policy choice.
While congressional Republicans talk about these cuts in the abstract, I’ve seen what they look like in real life. After more than 20 years as an OB-GYN, I’ve sat across from patients who were worried about the cost of their prescriptions. Patients who delayed care because they needed to put food on the table for their kids. Postpartum patients who, in the middle of caring for a new baby, were worried about how they were going to pay off their hospital bill.
I know exactly what these cuts cost — not in dollars, but in people's lives.
The only way to put an end to this cruel agenda and start making government deliver results that actually help Minnesotans and Americans is to take back the House this November by electing Democrats up and down the ticket.

Hey, it's The Collective PAC! We're reaching out because we're inviting you to join us at the Essence Festival of Culture on July 3rd and July 4th!
We have two events occurring in New Orleans next week, and we'd love to see you there! Please, take a moment to read more about our events below:
### **An Afternoon with The Collective PAC**
* * *
On Friday, An Afternoon with The Collective PAC is a chance to:
🔷 Connect with the nation's largest political action committee dedicated to electing Black candidates
🔷 Hear directly from founders Stefanie Brown James and Quentin James
🔷 Learn how to invest in Black political power ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.
It will be an intentional gathering of leaders committed to building and sustaining power for our communities.
**[You can click here to RSVP and join us on Friday, July 3rd, from 2:00-4:00 PM at the Loews Hotel in New Orleans (300 Poydras St.).](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/c336c428-d63b-4053-ab64-564dc832d426?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ RSVP HERE »](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/c336c428-d63b-4053-ab64-564dc832d426?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/90c135ce-8878-48b6-8d00-bf74363fd18b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
### **The 4th Annual Collective Power Brunch**
* * *
On Saturday, we hope you can join us for delicious food and cocktails at the 4th Annual Collective Power Brunch!
This dynamic event will bring together changemakers, leaders, and visionaries from across the country as we honor the legacy and resilience of Black leadership.
The 4th Annual Collective Power Brunch Honorees include:
* Ashley Allison, The Root
* Power Rising
* Rev. Shavon Arline-Bradley, National Council of Negro Women
* Mayor Steven Reed, City of Montgomery, AL
* Louisiana Legislative Black Caucus
* Damon Hewitt, Lawyers Committee for Civil Rights

**[You can click here to join us and The Vote To Live Action Fund at our Collective Power Brunch on Saturday, July 4th, at 11:00 AM.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/126e2e91-9f38-4261-a703-135e23e2d266?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ RSVP HERE »](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/126e2e91-9f38-4261-a703-135e23e2d266?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

---|---|---
### **Support The Collective PAC**
* * *
In 2026 alone, The Collective PAC has endorsed over 100+ Black candidates at every level of government.
We are strategically focused on creating a truly equitable democracy where our nation's local, state, and federal governments have diverse and talented elected leadership.
A truly equitable democracy means Black people are fully represented in positions of power - and are able to create the policies necessary to move our communities forward.
But we're not waiting for someone else to step in.
We're recruiting candidates, training leaders, investing in campaigns, and building the infrastructure needed to win races up and down the ballot.
And we depend on grassroots support to elect bold, Black Democrats who will stand up to Donald Trump and give us the representation we deserve.
Every dollar donated helps fund our voter outreach, candidate support, and campaign operations needed to build Black political power.
**[So, if you cannot attend these events in New Orleans, but you care about our mission of organizing, mobilizing, and electing Black Democrats across the country ... Will you please donate towards our efforts here at The Collective PAC today?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/ff5c46de-b5d9-40e7-9550-6218ddc6f519?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[DONATE $9 NOW »](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/ff5c46de-b5d9-40e7-9550-6218ddc6f519?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you!
The Collective PAC

subject: America’s 250th birthday

body:
It’s our turn to strengthen the fabric of our nation.

---
Peter, America will celebrate its 250th birthday next week. It can be easy to overlook just how incredible — and improbable — this milestone is. America has always been an experiment, defined by the belief that people united not by race or ethnicity but by a shared set of ideals can live and work together. We’ve seen the power of that belief over the last two and a half centuries. But our democracy has never been self-executing. At every turn, we’ve had to keep it alive. Revolutionaries, inventors, abolitionists, suffragists, civil rights leaders, entrepreneurs, and organizers have worked and sacrificed to keep us moving forward. Of course, there have always been people who don’t believe in the American experiment — leaders who put their self-interest ahead of the common good, and would prefer to take us backward rather than give up their own wealth and power. But generation after generation, the American people have prevailed. They’ve rolled up their sleeves, locked arms, and done the hard work of building a more perfect union. **Now it’s our turn to answer the call. ** **The National Democratic Redistricting Committee has a plan to defeat the gerrymandering that threatens fair elections so we can ensure that the will of the people ultimately prevails. We celebrate this historic milestone because it took heroism and sacrifice to get here. It took leaders who had a vision for what America could be — and who helped make it real.
Together, they believed in an America where everyone has an equal opportunity to make their voices heard. Where every person is equal under the law, no matter who they are or where they live. Where elections are always free and fair.
**250 years after America’s founding, that vision is still our north star. Attorney General Eric Holder and I founded the NDRC to protect the promise of America from the extreme, anti-democratic forces trying to undermine it.**
Right now, too many Republicans are trying to hold onto power and silence voters. They’re manipulating district maps to entrench themselves, while making it harder for ordinary citizens — especially in Black and brown communities — to elect the representatives they want.
**But in America, we the people get the final say. It’s our turn to roll up our sleeves and help strengthen the fabric of our nation.[I believe we will rise to meet the urgency of this moment. If you can, please make a donation to the NDRC, and let’s get to work.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134026313/629856244/1548394306?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_JuneObama_email_20260625-NDRC-Tier1-JuneObama_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260625-NDRC-Tier1-JuneObama_&utm_campaign=JuneObama&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjgwNDI2MzM2LWUxNzAtZjExMS1hYzljLTAwMGQzYTU0YmVkMCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=8JuPQw843mgEVj_dw0T_lpldEmMtk3_luJeTK9MurFE=)**

clean_body: It’s our turn to strengthen the fabric of our nation. Peter, America will celebrate its 250th birthday next week. It can be easy to overlook just how incredible — and improbable — this milestone is. America has always been an experiment, defined by the belief that people united not by race or ethnicity but by a shared set of ideals can live and work together. We’ve seen the power of that belief over the last two and a half centuries. But our democracy has never been self-executing. At every turn, we’ve had to keep it alive. Revolutionaries, inventors, abolitionists, suffragists, civil rights leaders, entrepreneurs, and organizers have worked and sacrificed to keep us moving forward. Of course, there have always been people who don’t believe in the American experiment — leaders who put their self-interest ahead of the common good, and would prefer to take us backward rather than give up their own wealth and power. But generation after generation, the American people have prevailed. They’ve rolled up their sleeves, locked arms, and done the hard work of building a more perfect union. Now it’s our turn to answer the call. The National Democratic Redistricting Committee has a plan to defeat the gerrymandering that threatens fair elections so we can ensure that the will of the people ultimately prevails. = | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = = | = = | = We celebrate this historic milestone because it took heroism and sacrifice to get here. It took leaders who had a vision for what America could be — and who helped make it real. Together, they believed in an America where everyone has an equal opportunity to make their voices heard. Where every person is equal under the law, no matter who they are or where they live. Where elections are always free and fair. 250 years after America’s founding, that vision is still our north star. Attorney General Eric Holder and I founded the NDRC to protect the promise of America from the extreme, anti-democratic forces trying to undermine it. Right now, too many Republicans are trying to hold onto power and silence voters. They’re manipulating district maps to entrench themselves, while making it harder for ordinary citizens — especially in Black and brown communities — to elect the representatives they want. But in America, we the people get the final say. It’s our turn to roll up our sleeves and help strengthen the fabric of our nation.= Thank you, Barack Obama = = | | Paid for by the National Democratic Redistricting Committee, John Bisognano, President. | | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|---|--- National Democratic Redistricting Committee 712 H St NE, #25 Washington, DC 20002 United States if you'd like to receive fewer emails from the NDRC. California Democrats,
As June comes to a close and we wrap up Pride Month [https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZ3ToQUhXch/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&igsh=MzRlODBiNWFlZA==] and Immigrant Heritage Month [https://www.instagram.com/p/DZQDBi8JRH_/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&igsh=MzRlODBiNWFlZA==] , we're reminded that progress happens because people fight for it. California Democrats will always stand with the LGBTQIA+ community and fight for inclusion and the right for all to love and live freely—and we celebrate the generations of immigrants who have shaped California and remain committed to protecting immigrant communities.
P.S. If you were forwarded this newsletter and want to receive them in your inbox going forward, click here [http://www.cadem.org] and scroll to the bottom of the page to sign up!
[https://d15k2d11r6t6rl.cloudfront.net/public/users/Integrators/04eaa6b2-88f4-43b4-b978-7bb0708f5838/412F544A32524E6948494C797470636E70587776545562436A58554E6C686E6A2F4D324F54507364445848352F774C43764C4E36447A486C6651583664617A2F/editor_images/OIA%20ICYMI%20Banner.png]
Last week, folks across California and the nation celebrated Juneteenth [https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZxkw6tpSLF/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&igsh=MzRlODBiNWFlZA==] — [https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZxkw6tpSLF/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&igsh=MzRlODBiNWFlZA==] marking the day freedom finally reached enslaved people in Texas. Today and always, California Democrats honor the centuries of struggles and triumphs of Black Americans and remain committed to the ongoing fight for equity and freedom.
At June's monthly organizing training last week, we learned the ins and outs of voter registration from trainer Maureen Forney with Field Team 6. Miss the training this month? Sign up [https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/875048/] and join our next organizing training on Tuesday, July 21!
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP35/1/80994/images/Compliance%20Training%20v2.jpg]
This week we also held a compliance training for Central Committees, which included important compliance reminders, reporting requirements, and best practices as we prepare for the final months leading into the General Election.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP35/1/80994/images/Screenshot%202026-06-24%20at%204.09.41%E2%80%AFPM.png]
We want to give a shout out to all of the organizations and clubs that applied for CADEM's Deep Blue Eric Bradley Grant. This grant—honoring Eric Bradley's legacy as a trusted organizer and champion for young people—was designed to empower the next generation of Democratic organizers to run programs focused on engaging young Democrats ahead of the midterms. Congratulations to our outstanding grant recipients:
* Black LA Young Democrats
* California College Democrats
* California High School Democrats
* Kern County Young Democrats
* Latinx Young Democrats of Sacramento County
* Modesto Progressive Democrats
* Orange County Young Democrats
* San Mateo County AAPI Alliance
* Triton Democrats
At last week's Rural Coalition training with Rural Urban Bridge Initiative ( RUBI [https://ruralurbanbridge.org/] ), we learned about the underlying causes of the rural urban divide over the past 40 years. Join us next Tuesday, June 30, for the second part of this training series [https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/971092/] to learn what progressive groups, candidates, and parties can do about it.

body:

# [](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/685?refcode=&t=1&akid=5042%2E898137%2Ett2vSL)
Hey,
We just launched our first ad — and I took a bit of a risk. I gave my team the green light to make a bigger buy than we originally had in the budget.
Poll after poll shows us beating my Trump-backed opponent and it’s made us MAGA’s number one target. The GOP is spending eye-popping sums to buy Michigan’s Senate seat.
If we don’t fight back before it’s too late, we could lose this race — and with it, our chances of flipping the Senate.
[**Will you donate today to help power our new ad buy? [ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Derek, we’ll be
quick.

Our finance team has been poring over the numbers all day ahead of Tuesday
night’s End-of-Quarter deadline — and they told us we’re at serious risk
of falling short if we don’t see a boost of donations from
Cresco.

Here’s the thing: The amount we raise here in June... doesn’t only impact
our campaign in June. If we fall short on Tuesday, that means we have to
pull back spending in July. And a pulled back July means fewer ads running
in August. And fewer ads running in August means fewer voters spreading
our message organically in September. And fewer voters spreading our
message in September means...You get the point.

But if we catch up before Tuesday? That means we’ll be fully stocked for
the final four months of the election. We’ll have the resources to run
every TV ad we need in October and fully invest in our GOTV programs in
the final hours before Election Day.

Team, my friends over at Resist Reclaim Rebuild said I could reach out:
I'm honored to share that I have officially become the Democratic nominee for Congress in NY-21.
I am grateful for everyone who has believed that a dairy farmer from the North Country could build something strong enough to compete in one of the most important races in the country.
When we launched back in December of 2024, I didn't do it because I wanted to be a politician. I did it because I love this community, and I believe the people here deserve someone who knows their struggles, because they've lived them too.
Over the last year, I've traveled this district, met with families, listened to workers, farmers, parents, veterans, and small business owners.
Everywhere I went, I heard the same thing: people are tired of being forgotten.
That's what brought us here.
But this isn't the finish line. It's the beginning of the next chapter.
The eyes of the country are turning toward NY-21. More money will enter this race. More attention will follow. The fight ahead won't be easy.
But I've never been afraid of hard work.
On the farm, you don't stop working because you've finished one job. You get up the next morning and start the next one.
That's exactly what we're going to do.
Will you split a donation of $25—or whatever you can afford— between my campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild to become a Founding Donor of our General Election campaign right now? Your early support is the fuel we need to build a winning infrastructure, hire organizers, and ensure our message reaches every corner of NY-21. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-blake]

Friend,

It’s the honor of a lifetime to represent Maryland’s Third District in Congress. I am humbled and grateful for the trust you have placed in me to continue moving this work forward. Thousands more votes will continue to be counted by our trusted election administrators over the coming days, but the margins show that I will be moving forward as your Democratic nominee for a second term in Washington.

I want to extend a sincere thank you to each and every person who knocked on doors, made phone calls, and stood with us. Thank you to our state and local partners, my team, my family, and my financé, Eric. Candidates do very little on our own – and this victory belongs entirely to the team we built together.

While this is a moment to celebrate, it is also the start of the next chapter. It is full steam ahead to November, when the stakes this fall couldn't be higher, and all eyes are on flipping the House of Representatives. We need to make sure we keep serious, hardworking leadership in office and send a clear message about the direction of our country.

We are gearing up to go to swing districts and do the important work on the ground to flip the House and win that critical majority. Will you join us? [http://mobilize.us/s/QHTGDA]

Sarah

Hi Peter,

I'll be honest, I don't usually write emails like this. Abdul and his
campaign team know more about the ins and outs of political fundraising
than me.

But I've been watching him work so hard lately, and I wanted to reach out
myself.

Abdul is running this race with his whole heart. Every single day he gives
his all — waking up early, traveling non-stop to meet Michiganders, and
doing everything he can to get his campaign’s message out there — because
he believes we owe our daughters and the next generation something better
than what we're leaving them.

But Abdul’s campaign has a $1 million fundraising goal to hit before the
end of the month, and I know it's been weighing on him.

He always knew running a 100% people-powered campaign would be a
challenge, but now, as millions of dollars pile up against Abdul, he can

subject: The opportunity
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Francesca Hong
body:
This is a big deal
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260625-2960)
Peter,
Every now and then, it really helps for me to take a step back and look at the stakes of the race.
This is our year of opportunity. We could pass universal childcare, pass an AI data center moratorium, and raise Wisconsin’s minimum wage for the first time in 20 years. We can tax the rich and fix our broken public school funding formula.
Wisconsin can get back on it’s feet after 16 years of Robin Vos and Scott Walker, elect it’s first woman governor, and put a democratic socialist in a governor’s mansion for the first time. Some have called this a “big deal”.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260625.aUG92f&refcode=em20260625-2960&t=1&akid=2960%2E105371%2EZu9tJ3)
_People are *very* excited to talk to us about our campaign_
We’ve got five days to our June end of quarter. This will be a HUGE decision-maker on whether we can turn this moment of opportunity into a lasting win for Wisconsin. As governor I will stand up to corporations, fight for all of us, and bring a service industry hustle to the governor’s mansion.
**[We need your support to do it - can you contribute $10, or more to help us win?](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260625.aUG92f&refcode=em20260625-2960&t=2&akid=2960%2E105371%2EZu9tJ3)**
The stakes couldn’t be higher but I’m ready to spring into these last 47 days with you.
Together, we can tax the rich, lower costs for working families, and build a state where every community has what it needs to thrive.
**[Donate $10 ››](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260625.aUG92f&amount=10&refcode=em20260625-2960&t=5&akid=2960%2E105371%2EZu9tJ3)**
With gratitude,
\- Fran

**D.C. Insiders, Billionaires, and SuperPACs fear the prospect of a guy like me becoming a senator.**

body:
2026 is our biggest year yet. Here’s why:
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260625-2&t=1&akid=3644%2E587540%2Eieixno)
**2026 is our biggest year yet, Peter.**
Let me tell you why.
Trump is demolishing the economy, dragging us into another endless war in Iran, and creating new crises for working people every single day. I don’t like jumping right into the doom and gloom in these emails, but we have to be honest about our current situation if we want a chance at emerging from it.
The right has been playing a decades-long chess game, investing in down-ballot races, stacking state legislatures, and systematically dismantling the rights and freedoms people have spent generations fighting for.
**And the Democratic Party is at a crossroads.**
There are too many establishment Democrats who are unwilling to meet this moment with the urgency, creativity, and moral clarity it demands. Too many of them talk about fighting for working people while taking money from the same corporations that bleed them dry. They write strongly worded tweets and perform empty gestures in a moment where playing it safe just isn’t good enough.
**We’re done with that.**
Leaders We Deserve exists to elect a new generation of leaders. Bold, fearless, energetic, working class progressives who don’t take a dime from special interests or corporate PACs. Leaders who have the backbone to do what’s right, not what’s safe. Leaders who come from the communities they’re fighting for and refuse to forget it.
That’s what we’re building. And it’s working.
**We’ve already racked up 21 wins so far, and we’re 42 endorsements deep this cycle.** Leaders We Deserve-endorsed candidate **Randy Villegas** just beat back $2.8 million in establishment money in a race that could determine who controls the House. **Mai Vang** took on an 81-year old who’s part of a 47-year political dynasty in Sacramento and came out on top. And our incredible candidates in Georgia like **Jyot Singh** and **Bentley Hudgins** are winning primary after primary.
The House majority is within reach. We’re going to flip state legislatures. And we have even more endorsements on the way. With our efforts to elect _better_ Democrats, we can make our majorities actually meaningful. But we have more races to back, and more candidates ready to prove that fearless, progressive leadership is how we win back the voters we lost in 2024 and change the face of power in the Democratic Party for good.
This is the moment we’ve been working towards, and we need you with us in it.
**[Will you pitch in $5 today to help Leaders We Deserve continue backing the fearless leaders this moment demands?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260625_2_biggest.ZMa7Cw&refcode=em20260625-3644&amount=5&t=2&akid=3644%2E587540%2Eieixno)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260625_2_biggest.ZMa7Cw&amount=5&refcode=em20260625-3644&t=21&akid=3644%2E587540%2Eieixno)**
Thank you,
David Hogg

There's a specific kind of math that has nothing to do with arithmetic. It's the math you run at the end of a long shift, or at 2 a.m. when sleep won't come: rent due Friday, the paycheck landing Monday, and no way to make those two dates meet no matter how many times you reorder the numbers. It's the exhaustion of working full time, multiple jobs, overtime... -- and still falling behind anyway. It's the quiet shame, helplessness, and fury of knowing that one medical bill, one car repair, one missed week of work could knock your whole life sideways.
You are not lazy. You are not crazy. And you are not alone.
For decades, Americans have been told that poverty is a character flaw -- that if people just worked harder, budgeted better, hustled more, they'd be fine. We've been told that giving people cash with no strings attached would make them dependent, that it would kill the work ethic, that poor people can't be trusted with money, that families need supervision more than they need stability.
What if that story was never based on evidence? What if it was just ideology -- and one of the most unlikely presidents in modern American history almost proved it wrong?
Let's go back to 1969.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/421b8801-b8fd-47db-9409-5cc2193ba2d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
## The President Who Almost Ended Poverty
On August 8, 1969, Richard Nixon went on national television and proposed a guaranteed income floor for poor families. Not a socialist. Not a campus radical. **Republican** President of the United States, Richard Nixon.
He called it the Family Assistance Plan. It would guarantee a poor family of four $1,600 a year -- worth somewhere in the neighborhood of $13,000 to $15,000 today -- with the benefit tapering as earnings rose, so it always paid more to work than not to. Crucially, it would go to the _working_ poor, not just families already inside the welfare system. As Nixon put it, the idea was to build a foundation under the income of every American family with dependent children, a floor nobody could fall through.
His chief architect was Daniel Patrick Moynihan, a lifelong Democrat who'd served Kennedy and Johnson before becoming Nixon's counselor on urban affairs. Moynihan had a theory of how to sell a guaranteed income to a conservative president: he told Nixon that "Tory men and liberal measures" had reshaped Britain a century before, and that a Republican president delivering what Democratic presidents had only talked about could do the same here. Nixon, who'd grown up genuinely poor, bought it.
The response was striking. Editorial pages, religious leaders, and even large parts of the business and labor world lined up behind it. Among voters who'd heard of the plan, Gallup found 65 percent in favor and only 20 percent opposed. **In April 1970, the House passed it, 243 to 155. The following year, it passed the House again.** A guaranteed income for American families had never been closer to becoming law.
## The Pincer That Killed It
Then it reached the Senate Finance Committee, and everything fell apart -- crushed from both directions at once.
On one side stood the conservatives. Several of the president's own party on the committee turned against his signature bill, egged on by warnings from Vice President Spiro Agnew that liberal Democrats would only use it as a stepping stone toward something far bigger. Committee Chairman Russell Long, a conservative Democrat from Louisiana, ran the numbers and argued the plan still let some families come out ahead by not working at all -- proof, to him, that it would gut the incentive to work no matter how it was dressed up.
On the other side stood the liberals and welfare-rights groups, and their complaint was the opposite: $1,600 wasn't nearly enough. The National Welfare Rights Organization rejected it as too stingy. Senator Fred Harris of Oklahoma, who had backed the plan for months, grew so frustrated with round after round of administration concessions that he turned against it too. "I am despairing more and more that it can be done," he told a reporter that fall. On October 8, 1970, the Senate Finance Committee voted 14 to 1 to kill it outright. Nixon brought back a revised version in 1971. It died again.
Conservatives killed it because they thought it went too far. Liberals helped kill it because they thought it didn't go far enough. And the working poor -- the people who needed a floor under their feet more than anyone -- got nothing. By one widely cited estimate, the plan as written would have lifted 60 percent of the people then living in poverty above the poverty line. Instead, it became one of the great near-misses in American policy, the law that came within a Senate committee vote of existing.
## The Data That Proved Everyone's Fears Wrong
Here's the part almost nobody remembers: we actually tested whether a guaranteed income makes people stop working, because the fear at the center of all that opposition was exactly that simple -- give people cash, and they'll quit.
So researchers ran the experiment. The New Jersey Income-Maintenance Experiment, the first of its kind anywhere in the world, gave thousands of working families a guaranteed income from 1968 to 1972 and tracked what happened to their hours. The most careful studies found that male heads of household barely changed their behavior at all -- work reductions in the low single digits at most, with several rigorous analyses finding no statistically meaningful change whatsoever. Nobody quit. Nobody disappeared into the couch. If anything, some families used the cushion to hold out for a better job instead of grabbing the first desperate one.
Manitoba's Mincome experiment, run in Canada from 1974 to 1978, found something similar and more revealing. Men worked about 1 percent fewer hours. Women worked about 3 percent fewer. The only group with a genuinely meaningful drop in hours was new mothers, who used the income to stay home longer with infants, and teenagers, who stayed in school instead of dropping out to help with rent -- and graduated at higher rates because of it. A later analysis of hospital records from the Mincome town found hospitalizations had fallen by roughly 8.5 percent, with a notable drop in mental-health-related hospital visits and accidents. People weren't getting lazier. They were getting healthier.
The fear was never supported by the evidence. It just didn't need to be, to do its job.
## What We Actually Lost
Think about what that means. We had the data. We had a Republican president's name on it, which should have made it bulletproof against the "radical socialist scheme" attack before that attack was ever launched. **And it still died -- not because it didn't work, but because too many people on both sides would rather lose than compromise.**
This is one of the oldest, saddest patterns in American politics: the people with the least power are told to keep waiting while the people with power fight over theory. Wait for the perfect bill. Wait for a better Congress. Wait for the next election, the next commission, the next pilot program -- while rent is due now, the brakes need replacing now, and someone working sixty hours a week is deciding tonight which bill gets paid late.
Because poverty isn't only a lack of money. It's also what a body in constant emergency mode does to itself -- the stress chemistry, the cortisol, the missed dental visits and deferred repairs and bad sleep that come from never being more than one bad week from disaster. Cash doesn't fix everything. But it fixes the cash part, and the cash part is not small. It's rent. It's groceries. **It 's the ability to say no** to an unsafe job, a predatory landlord, a relationship you can't otherwise afford to leave. It's the difference between an inconvenience and a crisis.
**That 's what a guaranteed income floor actually buys: not the end of ambition, but the room to exercise it.** A parent who can't afford child care is not fully free. A worker who stays in a dangerous job because rent is due in three days is not fully free. The Constitution doesn't promise the absence of hardship, but it does promise to promote the general welfare and secure the blessings of liberty -- and those aren't decorative words. They're instructions.
A floor beneath every family is not a ceiling on anyone's effort. It's the precondition, of basic survival, that makes real effort possible.
## Care. Courage. The Constitution.
The lesson of the Family Assistance Plan isn't that Nixon was secretly a hero. He wasn't, and his own rhetoric about "workfare" over "welfare" helped poison the well for everything that came after. **The lesson is sharper than that: America has been closer to economic sanity than we remember.** We came within one committee vote of admitting, on a bipartisan basis, that poverty is mostly just a lack of money -- and that the most direct way to fix a lack of money is to give people money, which encourages creativity, incentivizes ambition, and creates room for long-term planning and productivity.
This is why I believe in what I call a Dignity Budget for People and Planet: wages people can actually live on, universal healthcare so a single diagnosis can't bankrupt a family, child care people can access and afford, housing people can actually live in, and cash supports that are simple, direct, and humane instead of buried in paperwork designed to wear people down. We need a tax code that rewards work and caregiving instead of extraction and hoarding, and an economy where basic stability isn't treated as a luxury good only some families get to have.
Today, a guaranteed income is politically dismissed as radical, fringe, un-American. But the man who came closest to making it federal law was one of the most conservative presidents of the twentieth century. If Richard Nixon could see the sense in putting a floor under every family, I'd like to know what our excuse is now.
The data was clear in 1972. It's still clear today. What's missing isn't evidence. It's the courage to choose differently.
Care. Courage. The Constitution.
A floor beneath every family.
And a government that finally answers to the people it serves.

What if that story was never based on evidence? What if it was just ideology -- and one of the most unlikely presidents in modern American history almost proved it wrong? Let's go back to 1969. | | ---|---|--- The President Who Almost Ended Poverty On August 8, 1969, Richard Nixon went on national television and proposed a guaranteed income floor for poor families. Not a socialist. Not a campus radical. Republican President of the United States, Richard Nixon. He called it the Family Assistance Plan. Senator Fred Harris of Oklahoma, who had backed the plan for months, grew so frustrated with round after round of administration concessions that he turned against it too. "I am despairing more and more that it can be done," he told a reporter that fall. On October 8, 1970, the Senate Finance Committee voted 14 to 1 to kill it outright. This is something that we cannot afford to ignore – not only in my race to win re-election in CA-45, but for our nation's democracy as a whole.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134029319/629865100/1897980251?refcode=em-6.25.26-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiM2M1MmZjN2ItZWU3MC1mMTExLWFjOWMtMDAwZDNhNTRiZWQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=9D6Gv3qTu1p9N5HM-5N25i-3-exr2TlbxL2XBsR7nac=) | **[Donate](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134029320/629865101/1897980251?refcode=em-6.25.26-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiM2M1MmZjN2ItZWU3MC1mMTExLWFjOWMtMDAwZDNhNTRiZWQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=9D6Gv3qTu1p9N5HM-5N25i-3-exr2TlbxL2XBsR7nac=)**
---

That's right: Only three seats separate House control. Three seats stand between us and stopping the Trump administration's dangerous agenda.

**The margin of error is thin. And ultra-competitive races like mine will make the difference.**

I'm a Frontline Democrat, which means I'm considered one of the most vulnerable incumbents in the country. I flipped this seat by 653 votes in 2024, and the national GOP has been out to take this seat back ever since.

We can't let them win. Not when working families are barely scraping by as a direct consequence of Trump's policies and out-of-whack priorities.

body:
We really hope people.

# If you have every said - “How can I help you win?” This is it.
---
| |
---
|
---
| |
**We’re at a defining moment in this campaign.** We invested 13k in polling because we needed to know if there was a real path to victory. The results came back stronger than we could have hoped, they showed we have a genuine path to winning this primary- and the best chance at flipping the seat. (which we already knew)
But there’s a catch.That polling took nearly everything we had. And while many national organizations say they want to elect progressive veterans, moms, and working-class candidates, most won’t invest in campaigns until they already have hundreds of thousands of dollars in the bank.
We know we have to play out ads for people to win, and we've paid for some awesome ones- but we do need the money to get them out.
We know it won't take $500k-$1M to win this race- and know we get to prove them wrong.
We believe people—not corporations, not billionaires, not political insiders—should decide who wins elections.So here’s what we’re asking.If you’ve ever told me, “I’m rooting for you,” “I hope you win,” or “How can I help?” this is the moment.
We’re looking for **100 people willing to raise $1,000 each** from their own network over the next five days.That doesn’t mean writing a $1,000 check yourself. It means sending a few texts, making a social media post, and asking the people who know and trust you to chip in $10, $25, or $50.
We’ll give you everything you need:
• Sample text messages
• Social media posts
• Graphics
• A team ready to answer any questions
**All you have to do is ask.** If 100 of us each raise $1,000, we can inject the resources this campaign needs to compete and win.This isn’t just about funding a campaign. It’s about proving that ordinary people can out-organize big money. It’s about showing that working families can stand up to the political establishment and win.If you’re willing to be one of our 100 grassroots fundraisers. Let’s build something that proves people are still more powerful than money.

body:
Two upcoming fundraisers in Culpeper & Fredericksburg + easy ways to contribute now

| | | | | [|

**Dear Friends and Neighbors,**
The 2nd QTR ends soon, and the **FEC filing deadline is Tuesday, June 30**. This is our moment to post strong numbers and show that Team Ollivant is ready to **defeat Eugene Vindman**.
Here are two important upcoming fundraisers where you can help us build the resources we need to win:
**👉 Culpeper County Fundraiser – Monday, June 29****Hosted by Terese & Ed Matricardi** with co-host committee: State Senator Bryce Reeves, Nancy Sharman, Delegate Karen Hamilton, Reo Hatfield, Amy Johnston, Shermichael Singleton, Sally Underwood, Tom Underwood, and Larry Green[**RSVP & Contribute Here**](https://us.list-manage.com/lgoedfacrnz?e=14c77a6723&c2id=09489c9156c428bed3a67a2822595ae0)

**👉 Spotsylvania County Fundraiser – Thursday, July 23****Hosted by Kirsten & John Pruitt **with co-host committee: Lieutenant General (Retired) Bob Wood and Jack Bailey **at The Pruitt Residence**.[**RSVP & Contribute Here**](https://us.list-manage.com/NuedEpWSKAx?e=14c77a6723&c2id=09489c9156c428bed3a67a2822595ae0)

These events are excellent opportunities to meet in person as your candidate, hear my plan to restore fiscal responsibility, strengthen national security, and protect Virginia families, and directly support our effort to **defeat Vindman** this November.
_**Contributions made before the June 30 deadline will be reflected**_ in our official filing and help demonstrate the momentum we’re building across the district. _**Whether you can attend one (or both) events or support online**_ , your involvement is critical.
**For questions or details on either event, contact Tucker Obenshain at**[**ato@tuckerobenshain.com**](mailto:ato@tuckerobenshain.com)**or**[**info@dougforvirginia.com**](mailto:info@dougforvirginia.com)**.**
🇺🇸 Can’t make it to either event but still want to support our grassroots campaign before the June 30 deadline?

Thank you for standing with us as we fight to take back Virginia’s 7th District,
****

**Candidate for U.S. Congress****Virginia’s 7th Congressional District**

body:
I imagine that donating to a political campaign isn’t your top priority for today. However, I’m hoping there’s something I can say to make you reconsider.
|

---
Peter,
I imagine that donating to a political campaign isn’t your top priority for today. However, I’m hoping there’s something I can say to make you reconsider and chip in your first $5 to help me flip North Carolina’s Senate seat blue.
[**_If you don’t need convincing, you can click here to contribute.**_](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk704&amount=5&t=8&akid=1882%2E124072%2EBzXCyo)
The momentum behind our grassroots campaign is surging – **all thanks to people like you.**
You’re the reason experts have shifted this race further in our direction.
You’re the reason The New York Times reports that North Carolina is the best chance in the country for Democrats to flip a Republican-held seat.
You’re the reason we’ve been able to fight back against the Republican dark-money super PACs investing nearly $100 million so far to defeat me.
You’re the reason the chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee says that _“Roy Cooper has to go down in flames.”_
**Keeping up this momentum and winning won’t be easy, though. The GOP and its billionaire donors are coming after me with everything they have, and I can’t respond alone. I need your help.**
[**_Will you make your first donation to my campaign to flip North Carolina blue and take back the Senate for Democrats?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk704&amount=5&t=9&akid=1882%2E124072%2EBzXCyo)

Thank you for everything.
Roy Cooper
_If you've donated via check, mail or in-person event, thank you! Our system may not have processed your gift yet, but rest assured we have received it. Please note, if you have given through a spouse or another email or phone number, our records may not have transferred that information here. We are grateful for your support and no further action is required at this time._

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.
